Meet Royce White:

**Born and raised in the Twin Cities, Royce White was the son of a single mother and started playing sports at the age of 5 years old. Living in various neighborhoods growing up, much of his family remained in the Rondo community, where he spent much of his time and received schooling. White excelled at basketball and recieved a scholarship to play basketball at the University of Minnesota, and later transferred to Iowa State. He would go on to make Dean's List while receiving All Big-12 first-team honors and many other basketball awards.

_After being selected 16th overall by The Houston Rockets in the NBA draft, White began to voice concerns about the NBA’s collective bargaining agreement (CBA), specifically regarding mental health policy, which at the time did not exist. Eventually, his concerns became a public dispute between White and the NBA. This resulted in White demanding that the NBA, as a representative of the global corporate community, take up the responsibility of spearheading the mental health conversation – not just posturing through press statements, but through policy._

Royce then went on to win two championships in Canada before moving over to play Big 3 Basketball. White appeared at a game in a t-shirt that read “Free The Uyghurs.” After a game-winning basket, White did a post-game interview on CBS, where he called for 2 Million Uyghurs to be freed and released from concentration camps. As the season went on, White would touch on taboo topics such as Gain of Function Research, The Federal Reserve, Julian Assange, Edward Snowden, Larry Hoover, Jeff Fort, Muammar Gaddafi, The Great Reset, Ivermectin, Me Too, etc.

Now, Royce White is running for Senate in Minnesota to take down the Radical Left. Republicans have not seen recent success in Minnesota, but Royce's campaign is different: a grassroots movement that's sick of the Radical Agenda pushed by Far Left Democrats Tina Smith and Ilhan Omar. Royce needs your help to pull off a fourth quarter comeback victory and FLIP Minnesota Red for Republicans.

name: David Hogg
subject: I am never going to shut up about this
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
The housing crisis is one of the biggest challenges young people face right now.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20250421-1&t=1&akid=2021%2E587540%2E_ZmJTA)
Peter, the housing crisis is one of the biggest challenges young people face right now, and we _still_ have cities and states that are dragging their feet on doing something about it.
My family personally experienced the effects of this. When I was a kid we left California for Florida because the cost of living became ridiculously high. And now young people all over the country are delaying getting married, having kids, and starting families because it’s just not financially possible.
**That’s why I am never going to shut up about how much other cities need to follow the lead of Democrats in Austin on zoning reform.**
Austin has made more moves to make housing affordable and reduce homelessness than any city in America has in the past decade. They have enabled the building of so much housing and grown the number of rental units so significantly that rents in the city are DOWN 22% from 2023:
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20250421-1?refcode=em20250421-2021&:amount=5&refcode2=2021_587540__ZmJTA&akid=2021%2E587540%2E_ZmJTA)
We need more leaders on city councils, in state legislatures, and in Congress who see how successful Austin has been on this issue and will look to replicate their success in other cities.
More than anything, we need younger leaders at all levels of government who have _actually experienced_ the challenges young people are facing today, and who feel a sense of urgency to do _something_ about it.
**That’s why Leaders We Deserve exists. We’ve already elected young leaders to state legislatures and Congress from all over the country, and we have even bigger plans this cycle – but we can’t do any of our work without your support.**
**[So Peter, if you’re ready to elect young leaders who will actually tackle our country’s biggest challenges head-on, please pitch in $5 to support Leaders We Deserve today. We truly appreciate every dollar you give.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20250421-1?refcode=em20250421-2021&amount=5&refcode2=2021_587540__ZmJTA&akid=2021%2E587540%2E_ZmJTA)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

* **TOP NEWS**

"**Director of the embattled Texas Lottery Commission resigns as agency's controversy swirls,** " Austin American-Statesman's **John C. Moritz** \-- "The executive director of the embattled Texas Lottery Commission resigned his post Monday after a tumultuous one-year tenure leading the state's retail gambling enterprise, which brings in $2 billion annually to the state treasury.

The lottery officially [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/aec7bf54-a2e4-4870-84bc-719ec914db6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**Ryan Mindell's** departure without comment. **Sergio Rey** , the lottery's chief financial officer, was named acting deputy executive director, while the state agency determines its selection process for a permanent replacement during the governing board's April 29 meeting.

Mindell, who previously served as the lottery's deputy director and operations director, leaves behind an agency under legislative scrutiny and investigations by the [Texas Rangers](https://substack.com/redirect/f302921e-8a4f-437b-9068-a02fe2b4da75?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the Department of Public Safety and the Texas Attorney General's Office. Both investigations concern how the agency handled the introduction of courier companies.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $7/mo](https://substack.com/redirect/5f19be7a-e960-434e-8c65-a21dfc8fa5c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The high-profile resignation comes after the Texas House's unusual move to set the Lottery Commission's budget at zero for the two-year spending cycle that begins Sept. 1. Unless funding is restored during House and Senate budget negotiations, the lottery would likely be out of business at the end of August.

Mindell, whose annual salary according to [the Texas Tribune's interactive salary database](https://substack.com/redirect/6a28c955-d8a6-49f5-b250-e6b376779155?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was $225,584, took the helm at the 34-year-old state agency just a year ago after its previous director,**Gary Grief** , unexpectedly resigned. Mindell's initial months in charge were comparatively low key, but that changed when he appeared before the Senate Finance Committee in February, ostensibly to address questions about the lottery's budget request for the upcoming biennium.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $70/yr](https://substack.com/redirect/5f19be7a-e960-434e-8c65-a21dfc8fa5c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Committee members, however, focused on a controversy involving the Lottery Commission's acceptance of third-party companies that sell game tickets through smartphone apps. The state law that established the lottery in 1991 expressly forbids buying and selling tickets using a telephone.

The senators' questioning became heated after noting that a few courier companies sold nearly $25 million in tickets to a single entity, which won an April 2023 Lotto Texas drawing with a $95 million advertised jackpot and a lump-sum value of around $60 million. The sales were made in person, but the companies were able to print millions of tickets over a short period of time.

Mindell appeared to struggle to answer the senators' questions about whether he should have suspected the bundled purchases may have involved money laundering. Similar fiery exchanges played out when Mindell later appeared before the House Appropriations Committee and the Senate State Affairs Committee.

State Sen. **Paul Bettancourt** , R-Houston, suggested that Mindell's contorted responses to lawmakers' questions should be grounds for his termination.

"Quite frankly, if I was on (the Lottery Commission's governing board), I would vote to fire you," Bettencourt told Mindell during the director's Feb. 24 [testimony to the State Affairs Committee](https://substack.com/redirect/7e0a6950-9637-4fa7-95c7-6254fbb3e8b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)." **" The Jeff Roe Alamo**" Puck News' **Leigh Ann Caldwell** -- "All politics is personal for **Donald Trump** , and never more so than when it comes to **Jeff Roe** --the Republican mega-consultant whose once-massively successful political firm, Axiom Strategies, was effectively blacklisted by the president for, among many other things, having the temerity to work on **Ron DeSantis 's** money job 2024 campaign. After Trump's triumph in the G.O.P. primary, Roe went radio silent for the remainder of the cycle to protect his clients. In a post-primary conversation with Puck, he acknowledged that it had been "a mistake to run against a four-time indicted former president who was pretty well-liked."

So it was somewhat baffling when **Ken Paxton** , the controversial right-wing Texas attorney general, hired Roe earlier this month to help launch his Senate primary campaign against **John Cornyn** , a four-term Republican incumbent. Paxton is a more vociferous Trump ally, and the president has offered kind words in return. But in hiring Roe, Paxton may have jeopardized Trump's support in what is expected to be a nasty and personal primary, according to multiple people close to the White House. "This certainly has not strengthened Ken Paxton's hand," one of them told me. "Jeff Roe's involvement will hurt Ken Paxton more than help him for numerous reasons," said another.

The tension between Roe and Trump's team has been growing for years, particularly with Trump's 2024 campaign manager **Chris LaCivita**. Since reentering the White House, Trump's political operation has encouraged Republicans to blacklist Roe and Axiom and has made it clear he will not have access to White House personnel. People close to the president argue that Roe is wasteful with donor money--his DeSantis super PAC spent a record $130 million--and prioritizes payments over party. Even now, more than a year after DeSantis dropped out, Trump is usually made aware when a candidate has hired Roe, a person close to the president told me. "That guy does surgery on candidates' wallets," Trump has said, complaining that Roe's one-stop-shop, multiservice consultancy model is a racket. (The White House did not respond to a request for comment.)

Still, the Texas A.G. has his own history with Roe, whose firm helped Paxton during his previous campaigns, including a rough stretch in 2023 when he was impeached for bribery and abuse of office. (He was later acquitted by the Texas Senate.) His seemingly rushed announcement, which came earlier than party leaders expected, fueled speculation that Axiom had accelerated the timeline to secure the business. Axiom is also working for **John Bash** , who announced his candidacy for Paxton's seat as attorney general on the same day that Paxton announced his run for Senate. (A representative of Axiom declined to comment on whether Bash is a client.)

Roe, for his part, has assured people that he received an indulgence from the White House to take the Paxton job because of Paxton's relationship with chief of staff Susie Wiles, according to two people familiar with his comments. But a person close to the White House rebuffed the claim. It's "a classic Jeff statement," but it's "not true," this person said. "It's a flat-out lie." (A representative for Axiom denied that Roe has said any such thing.)

In any event, when Paxton went to the White House to notify the political team that he was going to challenge Cornyn, he didn't bring any representatives from Axiom, as would be customary for a candidate in that situation. Perhaps that's because Roe or other Axiom strategists wouldn't have been let into the building, people close to the White House told me. "They wouldn't even take the call," one said.

So far, Roe's engagement has not impacted Trump's endorsement decisions, a person close to Axiom told me, noting that the firm represented 41 of the 51 candidates that the president endorsed last cycle. But the Trump decree has impacted Axiom's business. In recent months, Axiom has laid off more than 10 percent of its staff--more than 30 people--and scrapped an employee stock option program that the firm had been working on. The Texas primary is sure to be bitter, personal, and expensive, costing up to $100 million, according to some estimates. If Paxton wins, a general election could cost double that. It would be a significant payday for Axiom either way. "They need that race," one Republican said of Axiom.

Naturally, the firm is trying to handle its comeback as delicately as possible. Though a source told me Roe won't be personally involved in Paxton's race, others familiar with Axiom's business say it's impossible that Roe would not have a hand in such an important contest. Either way, the acknowledgment that Roe must distance himself from the race suggests that he remains somewhat toxic in Trump's Washington. In an attempt to hedge his political bets, Paxton has started talking to other firms, two people familiar with the outreach said. But it's hard to see another firm getting involved in the drama surrounding the Axiom/Paxton-Cornyn showdown to come.

The Texas Senate primary, after all, promises to be costly in more ways than one. Trump has called both Paxton and Cornyn "friends of mine," and commented that the field isn't set. That's kept the door open for a number of candidates who are seriously considering a run, including Rep. Wesley Hunt, a military veteran who represents the Houston suburbs. (A supporter of Hunt said that he is "the solution to a really big problem in Texas" because of the Paxton-Cornyn-Roe kerfuffle. But many Republicans say that it's hard to see how he has a path if both Cornyn and Paxton stay in the race.)

So far, Roe's engagement has not impacted Trump's endorsement decisions, a person close to Axiom told me, noting that the firm represented 41 of the 51 candidates that the president endorsed last cycle. But the Trump decree has impacted Axiom's business. In recent months, Axiom has laid off more than 10 percent of its staff--more than 30 people--and scrapped an employee stock option program that the firm had been working on. The Texas primary is sure to be bitter, personal, and expensive, costing up to $100 million, according to some estimates. If Paxton wins, a general election could cost double that. It would be a significant payday for Axiom either way. "They need that race," one Republican said of Axiom.

Naturally, the firm is trying to handle its comeback as delicately as possible. Though a source told me Roe won't be personally involved in Paxton's race, others familiar with Axiom's business say it's impossible that Roe would not have a hand in such an important contest. Either way, the acknowledgment that Roe must distance himself from the race suggests that he remains somewhat toxic in Trump's Washington. In an attempt to hedge his political bets, Paxton has started talking to other firms, two people familiar with the outreach said. But it's hard to see another firm getting involved in the drama surrounding the Axiom/Paxton-Cornyn showdown to come.

The Texas Senate primary, after all, promises to be costly in more ways than one. Trump has called both Paxton and Cornyn "friends of mine," and commented that the field isn't set. That's kept the door open for a number of candidates who are seriously considering a run, including Rep. **Wesley Hunt** , a military veteran who represents the Houston suburbs. (A supporter of Hunt said that he is "the solution to a really big problem in Texas" because of the Paxton-Cornyn-Roe kerfuffle. But many Republicans say that it's hard to see how he has a path if both Cornyn and Paxton stay in the race.)

Trump's endorsement would obviously be crucial here. Paxton, despite his impeachment, has proved to be uncompromising as the state's top cop, and an aggressive defender of conservative policies on the border and school vouchers. Indeed, he is more natural fit for a Trump endorsement than Cornyn, a mild-mannered deal-maker who's worked hard to build a relationship with Trump. But the involvement of Roe is a real complexifier. "I think hiring Axiom exponentially increases the odds that the president not only stays neutral, but perhaps endorses somebody else in the race," one Republican strategist told me. A representative of Axiom called the chatter "consultant fever dreams."

The primary race is expected to get ugly, in part, because the candidates can't stand each other. Paxton dislikes Cornyn so much that forcing him out of his seat might just be satisfaction enough. Likewise, I'm told that Cornyn's primary motivation for seeking a fifth term is his loathing of Paxton, a man he can't countenance as his successor. It's a race that few people want, or think is necessary.

None of this is deterring Roe, who is more interested in saving his business than in saving a G.O.P. majority in the Senate. And according to the Republican operatives I spoke to, that's the essence of what's fueling anger toward him. Paxton and his red-meat brand of politics can beat Cornyn in a primary--a poll leaked in early April, in fact, showed Paxton ahead of Cornyn by 25 points in the primary. But Republican Senate leadership worries that he'll have a hard time winning the general election. There's a second part to that same poll, conducted by Fabrizio, Lee & Associates, that hasn't been reported until now. It showed Paxton polling basically even (or within the margin of error) against a generic Democrat, according to three people who have seen the poll--not great for a Republican in Texas.

The domino effect on fundraising and the Senate map could be devastating if Republican donors and political committees have to spend enormous sums to defend Texas, a state that should be a shoo-in. "Every dollar that we might have to spend in Texas, that's one dollar we're having to take out of Georgia or Michigan," one Senate Republican operative said. Another operative, albeit hyperbolically, compared it to the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand before World War I: an unnecessary event that had a long tail of consequences.

Plus, Paxton is already having trouble raising money, multiple Republicans say. Donors (and Trump) bailed him out during his impeachment because they believed his role as attorney general would protect conservative causes in one of the most important judicial jurisdictions. But few party leaders are excited by the prospect of funding a primary challenge that will only balloon in cost if they have to expend enormous sums to save red Texas." Moritz \-- "The executive director of the embattled Texas Lottery Commission resigned his post Monday after a tumultuous one-year tenure leading the state's retail gambling enterprise, which brings in $2 billion annually to the state treasury. The lottery officially Mindell's departure without comment. Sergio Rey , the lottery's chief financial officer, was named acting deputy executive director, while the state agency determines its selection process for a permanent replacement during the governing board's April 29 meeting. Mindell, who previously served as the lottery's deputy director and operations director, leaves behind an agency under legislative scrutiny and investigations by the in the Department of Public Safety and the Texas Attorney General's Office. Both investigations concern how the agency handled the introduction of courier companies. The high-profile resignation comes after the Texas House's unusual move to set the Lottery Commission's budget at zero for the two-year spending cycle that begins Sept. 1. Unless funding is restored during House and Senate budget negotiations, the lottery would likely be out of business at the end of August. Mindell, whose annual salary according to was $225,584, took the helm at the 34-year-old state agency just a year ago after its previous director,Gary Grief , unexpectedly resigned. Mindell's initial months in charge were comparatively low key, but that changed when he appeared before the Senate Finance Committee in February, ostensibly to address questions about the lottery's budget request for the upcoming biennium. Committee members, however, focused on a controversy involving the Lottery Commission's acceptance of third-party companies that sell game tickets through smartphone apps. The state law that established the lottery in 1991 expressly forbids buying and selling tickets using a telephone. The senators' questioning became heated after noting that a few courier companies sold nearly $25 million in tickets to a single entity, which won an April 2023 Lotto Texas drawing with a $95 million advertised jackpot and a lump-sum value of around $60 million. The sales were made in person, but the companies were able to print millions of tickets over a short period of time. Mindell appeared to struggle to answer the senators' questions about whether he should have suspected the bundled purchases may have involved money laundering. Similar fiery exchanges played out when Mindell later appeared before the House Appropriations Committee and the Senate State Affairs Committee. State Sen. Paul Bettancourt , R-Houston, suggested that Mindell's contorted responses to lawmakers' questions should be grounds for his termination. "Quite frankly, if I was on (the Lottery Commission's governing board), I would vote to fire you," Bettencourt told Mindell during the director's Feb. 24 ." After Trump's triumph in the G.O.P. primary, Roe went radio silent for the remainder of the cycle to protect his clients. In a post-primary conversation with Puck, he acknowledged that it had been "a mistake to run against a four-time indicted former president who was pretty well-liked." So it was somewhat baffling when Ken Paxton , the controversial right-wing Texas attorney general, hired Roe earlier this month to help launch his Senate primary campaign against John Cornyn , a four-term Republican incumbent. Paxton is a more vociferous Trump ally, and the president has offered kind words in return. But in hiring Roe, Paxton may have jeopardized Trump's support in what is expected to be a nasty and personal primary, according to multiple people close to the White House. "This certainly has not strengthened Ken Paxton's hand," one of them told me. "Jeff Roe's involvement will hurt Ken Paxton more than help him for numerous reasons," said another. The tension between Roe and Trump's team has been growing for years, particularly with Trump's 2024 campaign manager Chris LaCivita. Since reentering the White House, Trump's political operation has encouraged Republicans to blacklist Roe and Axiom and has made it clear he will not have access to White House personnel. People close to the president argue that Roe is wasteful with donor money--his DeSantis super PAC spent a record $130 million--and prioritizes payments over party. Even now, more than a year after DeSantis dropped out, Trump is usually made aware when a candidate has hired Roe, a person close to the president told me. "That guy does surgery on candidates' wallets," Trump has said, complaining that Roe's one-stop-shop, multiservice consultancy model is a racket. (The White House did not respond to a request for comment.) Still, the Texas A.G. has his own history with Roe, whose firm helped Paxton during his previous campaigns, including a rough stretch in 2023 when he was impeached for bribery and abuse of office. (He was later acquitted by the Texas Senate.) His seemingly rushed announcement, which came earlier than party leaders expected, fueled speculation that Axiom had accelerated the timeline to secure the business. Axiom is also working for John Bash , who announced his candidacy for Paxton's seat as attorney general on the same day that Paxton announced his run for Senate. (A representative of Axiom declined to comment on whether Bash is a client.) Roe, for his part, has assured people that he received an indulgence from the White House to take the Paxton job because of Paxton's relationship with chief of staff Susie Wiles, according to two people familiar with his comments. But a person close to the White House rebuffed the claim. It's "a classic Jeff statement," but it's "not true," this person said. "It's a flat-out lie." (A representative for Axiom denied that Roe has said any such thing.) In any event, when Paxton went to the White House to notify the political team that he was going to challenge Cornyn, he didn't bring any representatives from Axiom, as would be customary for a candidate in that situation. Perhaps that's because Roe or other Axiom strategists wouldn't have been let into the building, people close to the White House told me. "They wouldn't even take the call," one said. So far, Roe's engagement has not impacted Trump's endorsement decisions, a person close to Axiom told me, noting that the firm represented 41 of the 51 candidates that the president endorsed last cycle. But the Trump decree has impacted Axiom's business. In recent months, Axiom has laid off more than 10 percent of its staff--more than 30 people--and scrapped an employee stock option program that the firm had been working on. The Texas primary is sure to be bitter, personal, and expensive, costing up to $100 million, according to some estimates. If Paxton wins, a general election could cost double that. It would be a significant payday for Axiom either way. "They need that race," one Republican said of Axiom. Naturally, the firm is trying to handle its comeback as delicately as possible. Though a source told me Roe won't be personally involved in Paxton's race, others familiar with Axiom's business say it's impossible that Roe would not have a hand in such an important contest. Either way, the acknowledgment that Roe must distance himself from the race suggests that he remains somewhat toxic in Trump's Washington. In an attempt to hedge his political bets, Paxton has started talking to other firms, two people familiar with the outreach said. But it's hard to see another firm getting involved in the drama surrounding the Axiom/Paxton-Cornyn showdown to come. The Texas Senate primary, after all, promises to be costly in more ways than one. Trump has called both Paxton and Cornyn "friends of mine," and commented that the field isn't set. That's kept the door open for a number of candidates who are seriously considering a run, including Rep. Wesley Hunt, a military veteran who represents the Houston suburbs. (A supporter of Hunt said that he is "the solution to a really big problem in Texas" because of the Paxton-Cornyn-Roe kerfuffle. Paxton, despite his impeachment, has proved to be uncompromising as the state's top cop, and an aggressive defender of conservative policies on the border and school vouchers. Indeed, he is more natural fit for a Trump endorsement than Cornyn, a mild-mannered deal-maker who's worked hard to build a relationship with Trump. But the involvement of Roe is a real complexifier. "I think hiring Axiom exponentially increases the odds that the president not only stays neutral, but perhaps endorses somebody else in the race," one Republican strategist told me. A representative of Axiom called the chatter "consultant fever dreams." The primary race is expected to get ugly, in part, because the candidates can't stand each other. Paxton dislikes Cornyn so much that forcing him out of his seat might just be satisfaction enough. Likewise, I'm told that Cornyn's primary motivation for seeking a fifth term is his loathing of Paxton, a man he can't countenance as his successor. It's a race that few people want, or think is necessary. None of this is deterring Roe, who is more interested in saving his business than in saving a G.O.P. majority in the Senate. And according to the Republican operatives I spoke to, that's the essence of what's fueling anger toward him. Paxton and his red-meat brand of politics can beat Cornyn in a primary--a poll leaked in early April, in fact, showed Paxton ahead of Cornyn by 25 points in the primary. But Republican Senate leadership worries that he'll have a hard time winning the general election. There's a second part to that same poll, conducted by Fabrizio, Lee & Associates, that hasn't been reported until now. It showed Paxton polling basically even (or within the margin of error) against a generic Democrat, according to three people who have seen the poll--not great for a Republican in Texas. The domino effect on fundraising and the Senate map could be devastating if Republican donors and political committees have to spend enormous sums to defend Texas, a state that should be a shoo-in. "Every dollar that we might have to spend in Texas, that's one dollar we're having to take out of Georgia or Michigan," one Senate Republican operative said. Another operative, albeit hyperbolically, compared it to the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand before World War I: an unnecessary event that had a long tail of consequences. Plus, Paxton is already having trouble raising money, multiple Republicans say. Donors (and Trump) bailed him out during his impeachment because they believed his role as attorney general would protect conservative causes in one of the most important judicial jurisdictions. But few party leaders are excited by the prospect of funding a primary challenge that will only balloon in cost if they have to expend enormous sums to save red Texas." "**Director of the embattled Texas Lottery Commission resigns as agency's controversy swirls,** " Austin American-Statesman's **John C. Moritz** \-- "The executive director of the embattled Texas Lottery Commission resigned his post Monday after a tumultuous one-year tenure leading the state's retail gambling enterprise, which brings in $2 billion annually to the state treasury.

The lottery officially [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/6bd60f30-0da9-49c2-90bf-2113f5b98898?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**Ryan Mindell's** departure without comment. **Sergio Rey** , the lottery's chief financial officer, was named acting deputy executive director, while the state agency determines its selection process for a permanent replacement during the governing board's April 29 meeting.

Mindell, who previously served as the lottery's deputy director and operations director, leaves behind an agency under legislative scrutiny and investigations by the [Texas Rangers](https://substack.com/redirect/f8d7aacb-be67-4d88-8e46-9939e80704e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the Department of Public Safety and the Texas Attorney General's Office. Both investigations concern how the agency handled the introduction of courier companies.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $7/mo](https://substack.com/redirect/882e1e28-797c-4bab-b875-48fcc73d3211?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The high-profile resignation comes after the Texas House's unusual move to set the Lottery Commission's budget at zero for the two-year spending cycle that begins Sept. 1. Unless funding is restored during House and Senate budget negotiations, the lottery would likely be out of business at the end of August.

Mindell, whose annual salary according to [the Texas Tribune's interactive salary database](https://substack.com/redirect/55302e69-4c99-4353-a7a4-654acab240d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was $225,584, took the helm at the 34-year-old state agency just a year ago after its previous director,**Gary Grief** , unexpectedly resigned. Mindell's initial months in charge were comparatively low key, but that changed when he appeared before the Senate Finance Committee in February, ostensibly to address questions about the lottery's budget request for the upcoming biennium.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $70/yr](https://substack.com/redirect/882e1e28-797c-4bab-b875-48fcc73d3211?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Committee members, however, focused on a controversy involving the Lottery Commission's acceptance of third-party companies that sell game tickets through smartphone apps. The state law that established the lottery in 1991 expressly forbids buying and selling tickets using a telephone.

The senators' questioning became heated after noting that a few courier companies sold nearly $25 million in tickets to a single entity, which won an April 2023 Lotto Texas drawing with a $95 million advertised jackpot and a lump-sum value of around $60 million. The sales were made in person, but the companies were able to print millions of tickets over a short period of time.

Mindell appeared to struggle to answer the senators' questions about whether he should have suspected the bundled purchases may have involved money laundering. Similar fiery exchanges played out when Mindell later appeared before the House Appropriations Committee and the Senate State Affairs Committee.

State Sen. **Paul Bettancourt** , R-Houston, suggested that Mindell's contorted responses to lawmakers' questions should be grounds for his termination.

"Quite frankly, if I was on (the Lottery Commission's governing board), I would vote to fire you," Bettencourt told Mindell during the director's Feb. 24 [testimony to the State Affairs Committee](https://substack.com/redirect/f84fe39c-a9ff-43b0-b4bb-190785cf7dc4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)." **" The Jeff Roe Alamo**" Puck News' **Leigh Ann Caldwell** -- "All politics is personal for **Donald Trump** , and never more so than when it comes to **Jeff Roe** --the Republican mega-consultant whose once-massively successful political firm, Axiom Strategies, was effectively blacklisted by the president for, among many other things, having the temerity to work on **Ron DeSantis 's** money job 2024 campaign. After Trump's triumph in the G.O.P. primary, Roe went radio silent for the remainder of the cycle to protect his clients. In a post-primary conversation with Puck, he acknowledged that it had been "a mistake to run against a four-time indicted former president who was pretty well-liked."

So it was somewhat baffling when **Ken Paxton** , the controversial right-wing Texas attorney general, hired Roe earlier this month to help launch his Senate primary campaign against **John Cornyn** , a four-term Republican incumbent. Paxton is a more vociferous Trump ally, and the president has offered kind words in return. But in hiring Roe, Paxton may have jeopardized Trump's support in what is expected to be a nasty and personal primary, according to multiple people close to the White House. "This certainly has not strengthened Ken Paxton's hand," one of them told me. "Jeff Roe's involvement will hurt Ken Paxton more than help him for numerous reasons," said another.

The tension between Roe and Trump's team has been growing for years, particularly with Trump's 2024 campaign manager **Chris LaCivita**. Since reentering the White House, Trump's political operation has encouraged Republicans to blacklist Roe and Axiom and has made it clear he will not have access to White House personnel. People close to the president argue that Roe is wasteful with donor money--his DeSantis super PAC spent a record $130 million--and prioritizes payments over party. Even now, more than a year after DeSantis dropped out, Trump is usually made aware when a candidate has hired Roe, a person close to the president told me. "That guy does surgery on candidates' wallets," Trump has said, complaining that Roe's one-stop-shop, multiservice consultancy model is a racket. (The White House did not respond to a request for comment.)

Still, the Texas A.G. has his own history with Roe, whose firm helped Paxton during his previous campaigns, including a rough stretch in 2023 when he was impeached for bribery and abuse of office. (He was later acquitted by the Texas Senate.) His seemingly rushed announcement, which came earlier than party leaders expected, fueled speculation that Axiom had accelerated the timeline to secure the business. Axiom is also working for **John Bash** , who announced his candidacy for Paxton's seat as attorney general on the same day that Paxton announced his run for Senate. (A representative of Axiom declined to comment on whether Bash is a client.)

Roe, for his part, has assured people that he received an indulgence from the White House to take the Paxton job because of Paxton's relationship with chief of staff Susie Wiles, according to two people familiar with his comments. But a person close to the White House rebuffed the claim. It's "a classic Jeff statement," but it's "not true," this person said. "It's a flat-out lie." (A representative for Axiom denied that Roe has said any such thing.)

In any event, when Paxton went to the White House to notify the political team that he was going to challenge Cornyn, he didn't bring any representatives from Axiom, as would be customary for a candidate in that situation. Perhaps that's because Roe or other Axiom strategists wouldn't have been let into the building, people close to the White House told me. "They wouldn't even take the call," one said.

So far, Roe's engagement has not impacted Trump's endorsement decisions, a person close to Axiom told me, noting that the firm represented 41 of the 51 candidates that the president endorsed last cycle. But the Trump decree has impacted Axiom's business. In recent months, Axiom has laid off more than 10 percent of its staff--more than 30 people--and scrapped an employee stock option program that the firm had been working on. The Texas primary is sure to be bitter, personal, and expensive, costing up to $100 million, according to some estimates. If Paxton wins, a general election could cost double that. It would be a significant payday for Axiom either way. "They need that race," one Republican said of Axiom.

Naturally, the firm is trying to handle its comeback as delicately as possible. Though a source told me Roe won't be personally involved in Paxton's race, others familiar with Axiom's business say it's impossible that Roe would not have a hand in such an important contest. Either way, the acknowledgment that Roe must distance himself from the race suggests that he remains somewhat toxic in Trump's Washington. In an attempt to hedge his political bets, Paxton has started talking to other firms, two people familiar with the outreach said. But it's hard to see another firm getting involved in the drama surrounding the Axiom/Paxton-Cornyn showdown to come.

The Texas Senate primary, after all, promises to be costly in more ways than one. Trump has called both Paxton and Cornyn "friends of mine," and commented that the field isn't set. That's kept the door open for a number of candidates who are seriously considering a run, including Rep. Wesley Hunt, a military veteran who represents the Houston suburbs. (A supporter of Hunt said that he is "the solution to a really big problem in Texas" because of the Paxton-Cornyn-Roe kerfuffle. But many Republicans say that it's hard to see how he has a path if both Cornyn and Paxton stay in the race.)

The Texas Senate primary, after all, promises to be costly in more ways than one. Trump has called both Paxton and Cornyn "friends of mine," and commented that the field isn't set. That's kept the door open for a number of candidates who are seriously considering a run, including Rep. **Wesley Hunt** , a military veteran who represents the Houston suburbs. (A supporter of Hunt said that he is "the solution to a really big problem in Texas" because of the Paxton-Cornyn-Roe kerfuffle. But many Republicans say that it's hard to see how he has a path if both Cornyn and Paxton stay in the race.)

Trump's endorsement would obviously be crucial here. Paxton, despite his impeachment, has proved to be uncompromising as the state's top cop, and an aggressive defender of conservative policies on the border and school vouchers. Indeed, he is more natural fit for a Trump endorsement than Cornyn, a mild-mannered deal-maker who's worked hard to build a relationship with Trump. But the involvement of Roe is a real complexifier. "I think hiring Axiom exponentially increases the odds that the president not only stays neutral, but perhaps endorses somebody else in the race," one Republican strategist told me. A representative of Axiom called the chatter "consultant fever dreams."

The primary race is expected to get ugly, in part, because the candidates can't stand each other. Paxton dislikes Cornyn so much that forcing him out of his seat might just be satisfaction enough. Likewise, I'm told that Cornyn's primary motivation for seeking a fifth term is his loathing of Paxton, a man he can't countenance as his successor. It's a race that few people want, or think is necessary.

None of this is deterring Roe, who is more interested in saving his business than in saving a G.O.P. majority in the Senate. And according to the Republican operatives I spoke to, that's the essence of what's fueling anger toward him. Paxton and his red-meat brand of politics can beat Cornyn in a primary--a poll leaked in early April, in fact, showed Paxton ahead of Cornyn by 25 points in the primary. But Republican Senate leadership worries that he'll have a hard time winning the general election. There's a second part to that same poll, conducted by Fabrizio, Lee & Associates, that hasn't been reported until now. It showed Paxton polling basically even (or within the margin of error) against a generic Democrat, according to three people who have seen the poll--not great for a Republican in Texas.

The domino effect on fundraising and the Senate map could be devastating if Republican donors and political committees have to spend enormous sums to defend Texas, a state that should be a shoo-in. "Every dollar that we might have to spend in Texas, that's one dollar we're having to take out of Georgia or Michigan," one Senate Republican operative said. Another operative, albeit hyperbolically, compared it to the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand before World War I: an unnecessary event that had a long tail of consequences.

Plus, Paxton is already having trouble raising money, multiple Republicans say. Donors (and Trump) bailed him out during his impeachment because they believed his role as attorney general would protect conservative causes in one of the most important judicial jurisdictions. But few party leaders are excited by the prospect of funding a primary challenge that will only balloon in cost if they have to expend enormous sums to save red Texas." Moritz \-- "The executive director of the embattled Texas Lottery Commission resigned his post Monday after a tumultuous one-year tenure leading the state's retail gambling enterprise, which brings in $2 billion annually to the state treasury. The lottery officially Mindell's departure without comment. Sergio Rey , the lottery's chief financial officer, was named acting deputy executive director, while the state agency determines its selection process for a permanent replacement during the governing board's April 29 meeting. Mindell, who previously served as the lottery's deputy director and operations director, leaves behind an agency under legislative scrutiny and investigations by the in the Department of Public Safety and the Texas Attorney General's Office. Both investigations concern how the agency handled the introduction of courier companies. The high-profile resignation comes after the Texas House's unusual move to set the Lottery Commission's budget at zero for the two-year spending cycle that begins Sept. 1. Unless funding is restored during House and Senate budget negotiations, the lottery would likely be out of business at the end of August. Mindell, whose annual salary according to was $225,584, took the helm at the 34-year-old state agency just a year ago after its previous director,Gary Grief , unexpectedly resigned. Mindell's initial months in charge were comparatively low key, but that changed when he appeared before the Senate Finance Committee in February, ostensibly to address questions about the lottery's budget request for the upcoming biennium. Committee members, however, focused on a controversy involving the Lottery Commission's acceptance of third-party companies that sell game tickets through smartphone apps. The state law that established the lottery in 1991 expressly forbids buying and selling tickets using a telephone. The senators' questioning became heated after noting that a few courier companies sold nearly $25 million in tickets to a single entity, which won an April 2023 Lotto Texas drawing with a $95 million advertised jackpot and a lump-sum value of around $60 million. The sales were made in person, but the companies were able to print millions of tickets over a short period of time. Mindell appeared to struggle to answer the senators' questions about whether he should have suspected the bundled purchases may have involved money laundering. Similar fiery exchanges played out when Mindell later appeared before the House Appropriations Committee and the Senate State Affairs Committee. State Sen. Paul Bettancourt , R-Houston, suggested that Mindell's contorted responses to lawmakers' questions should be grounds for his termination. "Quite frankly, if I was on (the Lottery Commission's governing board), I would vote to fire you," Bettencourt told Mindell during the director's Feb. 24 ." After Trump's triumph in the G.O.P. primary, Roe went radio silent for the remainder of the cycle to protect his clients. In a post-primary conversation with Puck, he acknowledged that it had been "a mistake to run against a four-time indicted former president who was pretty well-liked." So it was somewhat baffling when Ken Paxton , the controversial right-wing Texas attorney general, hired Roe earlier this month to help launch his Senate primary campaign against John Cornyn , a four-term Republican incumbent. Paxton is a more vociferous Trump ally, and the president has offered kind words in return. But in hiring Roe, Paxton may have jeopardized Trump's support in what is expected to be a nasty and personal primary, according to multiple people close to the White House. "This certainly has not strengthened Ken Paxton's hand," one of them told me. "Jeff Roe's involvement will hurt Ken Paxton more than help him for numerous reasons," said another. The tension between Roe and Trump's team has been growing for years, particularly with Trump's 2024 campaign manager Chris LaCivita. Since reentering the White House, Trump's political operation has encouraged Republicans to blacklist Roe and Axiom and has made it clear he will not have access to White House personnel. People close to the president argue that Roe is wasteful with donor money--his DeSantis super PAC spent a record $130 million--and prioritizes payments over party. Even now, more than a year after DeSantis dropped out, Trump is usually made aware when a candidate has hired Roe, a person close to the president told me. "That guy does surgery on candidates' wallets," Trump has said, complaining that Roe's one-stop-shop, multiservice consultancy model is a racket. (The White House did not respond to a request for comment.) Still, the Texas A.G. has his own history with Roe, whose firm helped Paxton during his previous campaigns, including a rough stretch in 2023 when he was impeached for bribery and abuse of office. (He was later acquitted by the Texas Senate.) His seemingly rushed announcement, which came earlier than party leaders expected, fueled speculation that Axiom had accelerated the timeline to secure the business. Axiom is also working for John Bash , who announced his candidacy for Paxton's seat as attorney general on the same day that Paxton announced his run for Senate. (A representative of Axiom declined to comment on whether Bash is a client.) Roe, for his part, has assured people that he received an indulgence from the White House to take the Paxton job because of Paxton's relationship with chief of staff Susie Wiles, according to two people familiar with his comments. But a person close to the White House rebuffed the claim. It's "a classic Jeff statement," but it's "not true," this person said. "It's a flat-out lie." (A representative for Axiom denied that Roe has said any such thing.) In any event, when Paxton went to the White House to notify the political team that he was going to challenge Cornyn, he didn't bring any representatives from Axiom, as would be customary for a candidate in that situation. Perhaps that's because Roe or other Axiom strategists wouldn't have been let into the building, people close to the White House told me. "They wouldn't even take the call," one said. So far, Roe's engagement has not impacted Trump's endorsement decisions, a person close to Axiom told me, noting that the firm represented 41 of the 51 candidates that the president endorsed last cycle. But the Trump decree has impacted Axiom's business. In recent months, Axiom has laid off more than 10 percent of its staff--more than 30 people--and scrapped an employee stock option program that the firm had been working on. The Texas primary is sure to be bitter, personal, and expensive, costing up to $100 million, according to some estimates. If Paxton wins, a general election could cost double that. It would be a significant payday for Axiom either way. "They need that race," one Republican said of Axiom. Naturally, the firm is trying to handle its comeback as delicately as possible. Though a source told me Roe won't be personally involved in Paxton's race, others familiar with Axiom's business say it's impossible that Roe would not have a hand in such an important contest. Either way, the acknowledgment that Roe must distance himself from the race suggests that he remains somewhat toxic in Trump's Washington. In an attempt to hedge his political bets, Paxton has started talking to other firms, two people familiar with the outreach said. But it's hard to see another firm getting involved in the drama surrounding the Axiom/Paxton-Cornyn showdown to come. The Texas Senate primary, after all, promises to be costly in more ways than one. Trump has called both Paxton and Cornyn "friends of mine," and commented that the field isn't set. That's kept the door open for a number of candidates who are seriously considering a run, including Rep. Wesley Hunt, a military veteran who represents the Houston suburbs. (A supporter of Hunt said that he is "the solution to a really big problem in Texas" because of the Paxton-Cornyn-Roe kerfuffle. It's a race that few people want, or think is necessary. None of this is deterring Roe, who is more interested in saving his business than in saving a G.O.P. majority in the Senate. And according to the Republican operatives I spoke to, that's the essence of what's fueling anger toward him. Paxton and his red-meat brand of politics can beat Cornyn in a primary--a poll leaked in early April, in fact, showed Paxton ahead of Cornyn by 25 points in the primary. But Republican Senate leadership worries that he'll have a hard time winning the general election. There's a second part to that same poll, conducted by Fabrizio, Lee & Associates, that hasn't been reported until now. It showed Paxton polling basically even (or within the margin of error) against a generic Democrat, according to three people who have seen the poll--not great for a Republican in Texas. The domino effect on fundraising and the Senate map could be devastating if Republican donors and political committees have to spend enormous sums to defend Texas, a state that should be a shoo-in. "Every dollar that we might have to spend in Texas, that's one dollar we're having to take out of Georgia or Michigan," one Senate Republican operative said. Another operative, albeit hyperbolically, compared it to the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand before World War I: an unnecessary event that had a long tail of consequences. Plus, Paxton is already having trouble raising money, multiple Republicans say. Donors (and Trump) bailed him out during his impeachment because they believed his role as attorney general would protect conservative causes in one of the most important judicial jurisdictions. But few party leaders are excited by the prospect of funding a primary challenge that will only balloon in cost if they have to expend enormous sums to save red Texas." name: Hillsdale College via 1600 Daily
subject: Your 2025 Hillsdale College Calendar
body:
It is, therefore, completely unaccountable to “we the people.”.

This sponsored message from 1600 Daily is on behalf of Hillsdale College
| | | [](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2zpph2genf3q7h9e6f3v3m94594pk71r99eeb9keg_rp22sh2s8i6eob5cpi66o31cph2bs)
---
| | Dear Fellow American,

I'm reaching out to you today because I'd like to send you your **2025 Hillsdale College calendar**.

I know, I know. It's a little early to be thinking about 2025. But since you're someone who cares about liberty, I wanted to make sure you had this chance to get the 2025 calendar.

**Claim your 2025 Hillsdale College calendar before February 28 by clicking on this secure link:**

[**https://secured.hillsdale.edu/hillsdale/2025calendar**](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2zb52a1mm0if2uefgsa148ephjoi784l4ls8hm7ng_rp22sh2s8i6eob5cpi66o31cph2bs)

As you know, we live in an era of increasing bureaucratic despotism. You've seen it, and you understand. More and more, we are ruled by an administrative state that operates without the say of our elected representatives.

It is, therefore, completely **unaccountable** to "we the people."

This collapse of the separation of powers has spread far beyond the federal level into our states, our cities, and maybe even where you live!

One particularly disturbing example is in our K-12 schools...

At these schools, swarms of administrators impose dangerous ideologies and actively undermine parents.

In higher education--especially at taxpayer-funded state universities--bloated administrations push ideologies that teach young Americans to disrespect or even hate their country.

But thanks to our supporters, we remain free of this corrupting influence. We stay true to our mission...

...to provide "sound learning" that preserves "the blessings of civil and religious liberty."

Indeed, as the crisis in our nation has deepened in recent years, we have redoubled our efforts to extend this mission nationwide. But we've only been able to do so thanks to supporters like you.

**Just in the last year, our dedicated supporters have helped to ...**
* **Teach 4 million Americans in Hillsdale 's _free_ online courses**, including "Constitution 101: The Meaning and History of the Constitution," "The American Left: From Liberalism to Despotism," and our newest course, "Marxism, Socialism, and Communism."

* **Distribute hundreds of thousands of free copies of the Constitution** to citizens nationwide--especially younger Americans, especially thousands of K-12 students.

* **Provide an American classical education** to young students nationwide through K-12 education programs, returning excellence and proper civics instruction to K-12 classrooms.

* **Expand the circulation of _Imprimis_** , Hillsdale's monthly digest of liberty, to more than 6.7 million households and businesses.

I hope you'll claim your **2025 Hillsdale College calendar** so that when you use it next year, you'll remember how you can advance the important work of defending liberty through education.

Remember, your support is especially crucial because we refuse every penny of government funding--even indirectly in the form of federal or state student grants and loans. NOT. ONE. PENNY--to remain INDEPENDENT!

Your generosity, and that of tens of thousands of people like you, reaches and teaches millions of Americans nationwide. You'll help enroll millions more Americans in free online courses, expand the readership of _Imprimis_ , and restore excellence to K-12 education.

**Please show your support today by making your best tax-deductible gift of $50, $75, or $150 --or the best gift you can--by clicking the secure link below:**

[**https://secured.hillsdale.edu/hillsdale/2025calendar**](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2zepgavkuds16ivljs9shsrbop42gt36eu3lfqab8_rp22sh2s8i6eob5cpi66o31cph2bs)

And when you do, you'll claim your **2025 Hillsdale College calendar**. But you must act before February 28.

Thank you for being a steadfast Hillsdale supporter. Your generosity is needed now more than ever.

Warm regards,

Bill Gray, '01
Vice President
Institutional Advancement
Hillsdale College

P.S. **Claim your 2025 Hillsdale College calendar before February 28 at the secure link below:**

[**https://secured.hillsdale.edu/hillsdale/2025calendar**](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2zd191hafgipgjlag3p3u58l6kqhj420ktpb5nd8g_rp22sh2s8i6eob5cpi66o31cph2bs)

When you do, you will defend liberty and help us accomplish our mission year after year. **Everything we accomplish is only possible due to your continued generosity, so thank you for your support of our mission!**
---
| |
---

Pop Acta Media | 1600 Daily
---

"The 72 hour kit is a perfect starter kit for any scenario. Put one in your car, work bag, in your house or RV. If you want to start preparing safe food, this is where to start."_ _**Carol B.**

This is probably the cheapest survival food I have found, and the company is great."_ _**Gary M.**
"I actually had lost my job and was homeless for a while. I dug into my food supply, and I cannot fully describe how delicious and easy to prepare everything is. I felt like I was eating like a king. I am going to stock up again as soon as I settle into my new job. Everyone should participate with this company. You will not be disappointed."_ _**John H.**
"We're in Florida and have made many preparations for the aftermath of a possible hurricane. body:
The sheer number of college students turning out for our events was inspiring.

[](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI1MDQyMl9HSC03VS4xMTQ1MTBfdDE2Mjk3NTQtMzYyMyZleF90aWQ9MjAyNTA0MjJfR0gtN1UuMTE0NTEwX3QxNjI5NzU0LTM2MjMifQ/TsWdjN6IFlWA3G596Pz7tQ)Hi, it's Charlie Kirk again.
I'll tell you - the future is bright for the MAGA movement!
I knew young folks were breaking for the GOP even before Election Day. I could feel it in my bones. The sheer number of college students turning out for our events was inspiring.
Young men and women rejected the Joe Biden/Kamala Harris regime defined by rising prices, open borders, expensive housing, and blatant government waste funded by our tax dollars.
Now a new generation of Conservatives - inspired by our President - are rising up to meet this moment, including JD Vance, Donald Trump Jr., Republican influencers, Members of Congress, and MAGA candidates running in big races.
**One of those candidates is my friend, Vivek Ramaswamy. **
When Vivek told me he was running for Governor of Ohio, I was thrilled. I quickly invited him on my show to talk about why he's running and discuss how he'd work with the President.
He didn't disappoint.
Vivek talked about expanding our Party by slashing the state income tax, expanding school choice, cutting back property taxes, strengthening American energy, and bringing the heartland roaring back.
Young voters will love this platform. Our seniors will love this platform. Ohioans will love this platform. And anyone outside of Ohio will push for this platform in their own states.
Mark my words - Vivek's campaign promises will pop up in every major race this coming cycle.
[And you get to be a part of it from the very beginning.](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI1MDQyMl9HSC03VS4xMTQ1MTBfdDE2Mjk3NTQtMzYyMyZleF90aWQ9MjAyNTA0MjJfR0gtN1UuMTE0NTEwX3QxNjI5NzU0LTM2MjMifQ/Yfj2zNfv5oevRiOpzyAaUA)** That's why I'm personally asking you to support Vivek Ramaswamy's campaign today. It can be $4 or $400 - it doesn't matter how much you give. **
All that matters is that everyone reading this pitches in something.

You see, not everyone wants folks like Vivek to succeed.

The more "establishment" type folks prefer the company of the more traditionalists - the Liz Cheneys, the Mitt Romneys - you get the picture.

If you prefer the Republican Party going back to the old guard, Vivek is not your guy.

Thanks for hearing me out. God bless you!

body:
I’m all in on passing our MAGA agenda. Are you?

[](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/amPq/?__vbtrk=Mjg2NTA3OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=Mjg2NTA3OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)

**CONFIDENTIAL MEMO FROM TRUMP CAMPAIGN CO-MANAGER CHRIS LACIVITA**

[](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/amPr/?__vbtrk=Mjg2NTA3OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=Mjg2NTA3OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)

**[READ HERE](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/amPq/?__vbtrk=Mjg2NTA3OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=Mjg2NTA3OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)**

Friend,

When I served as a Marine in the Gulf War, I learned what it meant to fight for something greater than myself.

I shed blood for this country and was honored to earn the Purple Heart. But the fight for America didn’t end on the battlefield.

Today, I’m fighting on a different front – to defend our MAGA majorities, stop the radical Left, and build the war chest we need to win big in 2026 and beyond.

And let me tell you,
They’ll lie, smear, and do whatever it takes to stop the America First movement.

Believe me, I’ve seen this before. I was on the front lines of the Swift Boat Veterans for Truth campaign in 2004, when we exposed the truth about Democrat John Kerry.

## Pope Francis Dies at 88
[Pope Francis died early Monday morning](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO6yAQheGnwV2sYcCxU1Dcxl1uuyUCMyTsTsDCbKzk6VfeV9j6SJ90_o-rvbrEKd_-uweZFovNtG9MrVG1a1kpfmeqjld2-VY4bMXVzVkEHE6gT4g2uMQvq7tgIhGS6sjIUQ9KntWouru5KJyCIz15jOAJpdYawoAahglxjF0yhwYaUQKcpez9OAEuANNFqgv4IDRQSK3U_rOk3O4U-VWeVPulPDo299bWTah_AmeB877vvffLsQmcjzMCZ05PEjgv9StzfnN9h9ZVE9Y9MaftPAoNt4dL_Cu2P2V4GvwJAAD__ylecJM), at the age of 88, just one day after greeting tens of thousands in St. Peter’s Square with a final Easter blessing. The Vatican confirmed the cause was a stroke that led to coma and heart failure. See the [Pope’s life in photos](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuxCAQRL8Gd7ZgwcYuKNK4u7QprTUsd0QYLMyddX8fOVX6dLsz0ozefN2WG4YY0v0TNzLV5yXReUSqlcqy5538M1HBuEdM9xzdkbEcuACHvuWqBVgchvheVOOMJwKSDRmhVS_FILVsHmYUClFr51cvJ2engU-KEwDhOPaiF00wVxpXAILzQYhu1SMHy_k4CTnx1THFyYWaS_edQ6oP8vGdX1Q6m7cmmket-8HkB4OZwXyeZ5dWe1FcPoP5OhnMF0zrCyYbrjcGT-1frd2Drc9CR1tsQqF6paemGLefIcZwDJopft8wxN_a-q-tXgZ-AgAA___QlH3w). Francis’ body was placed in a coffin last night, with public viewing at St. Peter’s Basilica expected to begin midweek. The funeral is [expected to take place later this week](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGypCAQRb8GM62mUdGAYBOy2XRDC6UZ2WLEAmYs__4Vr94fvKyDU33vuf8ey8P44I_nX_MiVVxcDrpyoFIoLWc8yb0PSiacwRzPGGyOJmWzIODQQt8iLtb4cC99Y5UjQhINKS77QfBRSNHsSgzj5oyc3DoKwVcJRvKBy2EbxnES89Z4Vb9Bj8gBRs67VU6AG8A0czHDalkPZH2Jqfsf_VF2cuGOH0rdFl9NUHspZ2biD0PNUF_X1b2zKdGauwIMdS4x3Qx1NatETMEy1DWVoYa-3pyhrrqtS-bYfG5_vNu87WTfgRjqSfBZDDgBSIa6Scqelw_B51GyHp4v48N3pfKrHT8KvwIAAP__mdaDRg). With his passing, the Church enters the _sede vacante_ —the “vacant seat” period—setting the stage for the College of Cardinals to elect a successor. [The secretive conclave](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u5CAMhZ-GdIyMIT9TUGyTbrbdMnKCmbBiICJsZuftr7ivcDtblj-d7_x5LA8KMaTnb3qxrT4vid9n5Fq5LEc-2P9LXCgekdIzR3dmKictCNhLMBJxcRTiZzGds54ZWXds1Wh6rQY96m633k2-V5ocaN7UCupuUPVmGEbfr85PXbCNBgZRAQxK3dZxAtwAprvSd1idMMAu1Fxuf3NIdWcfP_nictvyq4t2r_U4hf4lcBY4p8-Rz9pOAucGFjiDabMSOL9ziU42xbbsWb5DjHJlmfh_lc1Xkq9cpC-UtnDKi2rYKMktpy3SxQLnrlh3tL9wDqMw8HxRiN9Z6o8KvCx-BQAA__88eoPI), held in the Sistine Chapel, is expected to begin 15 to 20 days after Francis’ death. _**Editor’s Note:** Several readers noted that Monday’s edition covered the Pope’s Easter message without mentioning his passing early that morning. The email had been scheduled the evening before; the news broke overnight. Thank you for your understanding._
## Resale Market Surges as Dow Sinks
The Dow [fell nearly 1,000 points Monday](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L_OozAQBPCnMR1oWZt_hYtr6HLtlWhtL8EXg5HtBOXtPyWv8HUjjfQbaf7dlhv54I_7X9pZlzUuB185cCmcljOevD4PThTOQMc9BpcjpUwLAnY1qBpxceTDe1GV0yszsqxYt4PqZNvLQVabXsmO3PdqQmUNdGRM37GR1AHiMHZT5fVHA4XYAvRt25hhBLQA49TKCYwTCtj5ElPzP_qjbLyGd3xxamzcq6C3Us4s5B-Bs8D5uq7GHsZ-SoHzhxY4g_pmgXMu0T7qndKDS12io3cd_Ivr5-mocG62socqaXdePgSf-0EouO_kw3et_Oqil8afAAAA__99EHkt) after President Trump escalated pressure on Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, calling for immediate rate cuts. Tech stocks led the decline, with Nvidia off 5% and Amazon down 3%. Meanwhile, with tariffs impacting the cost of imported goods, consumers are turning to secondhand markets. Resale platforms like Back Market reported a [threefold jump in sales](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OhCAURp8GOwxc8a-g2MZutt3SXPGi7CAYYMbM229mXmG7k3zJyZfzc5tv6LwL2zcepIuNc6AreyqF0nzGk-wjUEJ_egxb9GuOmDLOIKDlQnGAeUXnX7OqVm2JgJqKtOxV28iu6Ztq18qQXY2iEdseJI2DbCxAN4ztMtgWx8rpt00oAClEJ2W99IMAI8QwymYUy8qUoNWVmOrf6ELZyfpXfFKqTTwqr_dSzsyaLwYTg-m6rtqExbxHBtNbzWAS6sMMpgXNnR-Y7lS4ochLehwnL5ictZlv7kkcD0rOYMjc7BgM8RI_tBHfcXEl13s5fJX0el7Oe5e7nimxHej851L5V8enhr8AAAD__yoohtw), and apps like Poshmark and ThredUp saw increased traffic. The U.S. [secondhand apparel market](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2u4yAURldjd7bgQjAuKKZxl2mntPi52MxgsIDEyu5HeS87eO3R0fdJ5899vesQQ9p-6wNV83lNeNWIrWFZz3yifyQsOp5Rpy1HV7MuVa9A4DYQPgCsTof4WnnvlEcEZD0qOvEbo4JNrN8Vp5JKY4BKI6ibrbd8JkwyIa2-ceP7oN5rhANQQgSlo5kkAUuInCmbiXEdJ-hCy2X8m0NqO_r4yk8so81HH9Xe2lk79quDpYPluq7R5h0Lpnbo8g9bSDVse6tvvYPlGw4f2sFS0D-KCXVHN2BE20pOwdbhIwoqRF-UO68QY6hi6jjZDh3i1337UbOngv8BAAD__8EagpQ) is projected to reach $74 billion by 2029, growing five times faster than traditional retail. The refurbished electronics market is also expected to grow at a compound annual rate of 10.2% through 2032.
## Space Legend Returns to Earth at 70
NASA's oldest active astronaut, Don Pettit, [marked his 70th birthday](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGO2zAQheHTUB2N0VA27UJFGnWbNqUwEsciE5pDkLO70O0D5wrpHz48_L8-1g9KOZXjJ7141qeshb97ZlVua5XKz8_CjXLNVA7JoQu1TisCXi1MFnENlPK5TkOYn8zIbuB59NPVjTfn3RBnxw-cxqt3V_AB7gGC9_t-d-C3G_H2GNL81mBCHAFu43jZ_B1wB7g_RveALZgJOCSVdvktqWjkZz7li9tll9eQ56hau3E_DC4GF2lbUsoqgc73wODy5g0uMBlcRm9wKdTJUtcmNYrK0ajG02Y-uAQbpNjKqkltY_1spduN9j9WxTI1jVaKjalbDxrtlprGQOfQ5lC_U86p37yZ4HhRyv_-6X9F_ZrxbwAAAP__PjWL9A) on Sunday by returning to Earth after a 220-day mission aboard the International Space Station (ISS). Pettit has logged over 18 months in space across four missions in his 29-year career. NASA reports Pettit is in good condition and en route to the Johnson Space Center in Texas. [Follow his Instagram here](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOrCAUgOGn0W4MHFTGguImN3az7ZbkKAdlg2Dg7Jh5-83sK2z_5yv-z4d9YIghbR94kGGfbaKrRmKmYs98kv9OVDCeEdOWo6sZS0ULAoab6G8A1mGIL9u3zngiINWSkboflByVVu1utAKa1Lp6PUwr3QdaFidRKi1xlN4vbTBvTfQAUohRym7RdwGrEPdJqkksrukFucC5dF85JN7Jx1d-UunWfLTR7MxnbdS_BuYG5uu6upAq41bweBcNzFi5ZHsSc-B3peY9Nuo_pbYYd14hxlBH3fRiOzDEX5b_9OJp4CcAAP__WSFzJA). He and his Russian crewmates orbited Earth 3,520 times, traveling more than 93 million miles while conducting research on water purification, plant growth, and fire behavior in microgravity. Known for his passion for [space photography](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHOnDAQBOCnMZ2RvfgOKFykofvTpkQLXsCRsZF379D_9tFFeYPUo_k0ml9f8xfGFPP-E0_yspU5082JRKjOV7loe2WqmK6EeS8pcMHKOIOBhzZOA8wBY_qeXRP8RgTUNeRt7x6dfXZ91xweVnCjhYVowN49wgKDszBi3z1pcDQ00X804wCsMU9r26UfDKzGDKPtRrME5QyFKKW2v0vMctCWvsubaruWs0n-ELlYdT8UTAqm-77bjIztXt4KpjMyx5JZwcSCEktWMEVmXYkJ63p8gjVSXkmfRMIaq-gPoJGllowv0aFkfZFIFC2vmlnLQXrFkyrqkvW_voKpqT5cd0wp8rNXzuwnxvR3pvzXt28PfwIAAP__nTKQYw), Pettit captured and shared stunning images of Earth, including auroras and rare atmospheric phenomena like sprites and blue jets.

# [Ancient bakers used bread stamps to prevent forgery.](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sv47mr&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com)
### [World History](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sv47mr&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com)
[](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sv47mr&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com)
| I n ancient Rome, most people didn’t have their own ovens. This [included some bakers](https://track.historyfacts.com/?xtl=bem9cqsjdohtprba2jca1dreff27tuftnqwwtr61prderuf98ldwpegpi0cvi51iouuupudwnvjffca7bv5luwv77skga87pzbtkamgna125sm6nzcvfgql49de3wrbopcjxmzn9hsixlengcnadplchx4g2mt3cmwp1id70qtxm4x9ljtmonekzud2866sd7astkly7kw3fm53q0y9lj6yitd74b1jc3uo4z5ramt7hvuhnmu07cjm5rpqp62pnrqlm6oyav8f1qnouzpp0lk13lwt2yw0hte&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sv47mr&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com), which put them in a tricky spot since bread was strictly regulated. Government officials would carefully inspect the weight, size, and cost of the loaves, and nobody wanted to get punished for someone else’s substandard bread. So to distinguish their goods, bakers put their dough in the oven with a bronze brand on top, which would leave an indent on the finished product — not unlike a maker’s mark on [ceramics](https://track.historyfacts.com/?xtl=o3vgcqsyfn3hdx0ndejx4uv1jut1bvd66icu1473xsvfjxjiifppvpmjg0ofnpui8w94ynylmsdbck1p058vze9j8riws2x06tsv7wy518zol7u0xfco01ofj6fg6uh0kt7uck9ce6yr3h6mkv4mr7i4nrtpy0hmx6w2hlhap3lik1bg56uumskrtbdfwg7lmw318841mertd9ugzmh2aoag9qchb40ifqjwqifyvtvqpx4juzk2wrb2o5dtgzn6nnn8b30qn19&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sv47mr&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com). Some of these ancient loaves were [uncovered](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sv47mr&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com) at [Pompeii](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sv47mr&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com), the markings perfectly preserved in the volcanic ash.
---
While bread stamps were in particularly wide use in ancient Rome, the Romans didn’t invent the practice. Clay bread stamps have been found in various regions of Europe dating to [at least](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sv47mr&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com) the Neolithic Period. Many stamps were decorative, particularly for religious rituals. Early pagans used stamped bread as offerings to gods or to ask for blessings. In some cases, decorative bread could stand in for a more expensive sacrifice, such as an animal.
One stamp from the Byzantine Empire was used to mark bread as kosher. Orthodox Christians also began [stamping bread](https://track.historyfacts.com/?xtl=107jrez3mcm31on0oah737zdl0rcsvt76f6xfpf1l3mb44sdy4qhr8eaz1hqn801npyg7v732p15i2nm5dunfq0uobqg80oni3x33kyup9xd4dbmeitl6sko3gxchd2nl0gbwi9k2i9rjqybmejxh6luszpewcrs7qf0mxfyfsfr9y8et4m2soa734nm2p9vf1nebsszg160w34glgkjsox8pylpo8p18ajw3zxxfjwt59zg6mm6mcsrzpo4mm2bedn2vn5d70mkveim8w5tsivl199ehbjjakkvjk&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sv47mr&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com) for the [Eucharist](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sv47mr&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com) (including Holy Communion) or for saints’ feast days. Today, bread stamps aren’t as common, but they’re still a key part of some traditional bread-baking, such as [_obi non_](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sv47mr&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com) in Uzbekistan. Stamped bread or wafers are also widely used for the Eucharist in Christianity, and home bakers occasionally use stamps for Instagram-worthy sourdough.

## Ancient Romans visited fast-food counters.
Ancient Romans didn’t have [fine dining restaurants](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sv47mr&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com) like we have today, but they did have businesses comparable to bars, inns, and even fast-food restaurants. _Thermopolia_ were snack counters that served hot food to go. These establishments kept cold foods such as lentils, nuts, and meats in jars embedded in the counter, and the food was then scooped out and heated up for customers. A modern replica of a _thermopolium_ — though without actual food service — opened to the public in Pompeii in 2021.

## El Paso Shooter Sentenced to Life
Patrick Crusius, 26, the gunman who killed 23 people during a 2019 shooting at an El Paso Walmart, was [sentenced to life in prison](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAMhp8mdBklnkAmRYpr0u21VyJDDEQKBBHPsrz9iXmFrezC-j7__7-v_gtTTtv8F1fy_DOVfqOzZmKmo89pokob0zZSTFup-D5iqmPpQUErlZEAfcSUr9400Q8qOt2Q19a0T-2scs3i7aDwhaAx6o5G91JOd9aMBqGDNnauSf6GKQOgtdKmfagXamPdOE1GDwOCMIpi4nI8eCGmH6xTvso3HY-xrE32C_NexfOPgCAgnOf5eFfkEvG6DwSEyuW4BIQ72T2QU9kEhNsrIChz71pAoCx3rEV-JLIupXDaZnliXvFguWfCWOX8Tplv3uupXWu0VcoKCM3h436mnFPtrDBqXjHlz4v8u2K_PfwPAAD__x85iuY) without parole after pleading guilty to state charges of capital murder and aggravated assault. On Aug. 3, 2019, Crusius [drove nearly 700 miles](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOhCAURb8GOww8UYeCYhu72XZL85CnkiAYYcbx7zfuL2x3k5vcm3N-nuMTffBx-caNTPnMaYx05kCl0DEGP1OmWChO5HxMGV-H83lKIwhouVAcYHTowzWqyhkrnJYVGdmrtpG6F7pajZqEbXXfWN1B73QjBKFVWjTCPrDrdOXNPSYUgJRCqrYWD5Sq19M8K2ktAlOCnC_pqMtKhT6Y53ClNx31lLYqmLWUPbPmi8HAYDjPs55svinunsFwRwYDBb5jTvzEsOFReF5TKj4ufHnFDSNfXj6Ui--BkMFQHcbtpw_B565nSiwb-vB3WP6n6W3gNwAA__8uAn2J) from his home in Allen to El Paso. Minutes before the attack, he posted a manifesto in which he described himself as a white nationalist, motivated to kill Hispanics for immigrating to the United States. District Attorney James Montoya, the fourth prosecutor to oversee the case, announced last month he would [not seek the death penalty](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL0SnSAUhJ8GOxw44lUKijR2N21KB-GoZ4LgAN6ft8-YmTxBuq32229_PeenpUBx-2kPNPWzpjniuwSsFfMcaMWCsWJ06CmmYq_sqbg0g4CeC8UBZm8pfGfVeLMIr2WDRg6q76QehG52g_3qRA-jf4hxBN3p1alx8Y-uV92AGhoyd5lQAFIKqfpWjFaqQbt1VXJZLDAl0FNNua07VvzYsoZvemFuXTqaYPZaz8K6HwwmBhOG05Z02FugtClvDKYbwGAS6s6SwXTamsn95i5fha7Ct4tC_fLbl1PkZ6aSIv-nzu218Y6DkJq_bThsrvywpfCyp1Qp3ogmG3--KQQqj4EpsR2Wwt-B9f9ufRn4EwAA___Qu4xn) in an effort to provide closure to the victims’ families, who he claimed “want this case over and done with as soon as possible.” More than 40 people signed up to [provide victim impact statements](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunDAQRb_GdF7ZXhOgcJGG7qVNiWbxGEYZbGTPY3f_Ptr8QuorXZ1zfn8tX0BMefsFBwZ5pbJkfDZGEawLU8KGWTCvGCmXBt81UlvL4ozrtfHauSUC8XvxXQwPEyfbYbCD7-92GszU7cHjNE4-JtP3d2PtOBp8QBqiGUab7j52FD5nxjtnrbG-v5kRrB-mNSVvHw9wyhuMJKXeZEfBF7TE73Jhva3l6DjsImdT95_KzcrNf1J5yfWZlJs_LsrNXFZg5WZkfUIrOsFBTNh0ohx1k4p5k11DjjqVutGFGVvTkASrfgIfUEW3vRTB2vT2TSxvfTJCV0M8n8RM7cegvNkOIP6HJf8X8wrubwAAAP__e-KMlg), which are expected to last until Wednesday.
## Dinosaur Fossil Discovered in Big Bend
Students from Sul Ross State University [discovered a fossilized vertebra](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2uqzAQRldjOiJ7MCEULl5Dl9feEhk8hpGMHXkmf7u_SrZw-0_f0Tk_1_nqKVHe_vsDnbximTM-OaEI1jlRRMYsmFcMlAv7ew3Ea5lBQ99q2wLMwVN6z7YJbtFhNA06M9i-M-Ogx2Z3oY8-Lku_nDvQ1lxGABw6iwNo25lLaMh9zrQFMEYb25_0xRs7jGuM1iyLB2U1BpJST7Kj4MtzTO_ywHpay9Ekt4vcWHX_FEwKJsqCFVkob5g3yoiV8vaZKph4pY-Lgsknf3x97tzGwkypvWf0VXYMLeX2y2mqC7cnpUR8HpTV2-Epfanyt1YPB78BAAD__4lWgNI) from an Alamosaurus in Big Bend National Park last month. The long-necked, whip-tailed sauropod is the largest known dinosaur to have lived in North America, measuring an estimated 70 feet in length. The fossil is believed to be part of one of the region’s [most complete Alamosaurus skeletons](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDHOozAQRk8DnZFtbAiFi23osu2WyNhDGMnYkWcIye1Xmz3C33_69N77c1_uHhPmx29_gOP3VpYMFyVghrok3IAgM-QAEXMhf9aIFMqipbZCGqH1Ej2mz2La6FYZJ9WCU6OxvZpGObW7G8YAdoyjlVGFeJtCv1oIg70p6K0ZthbdvzNptFZKKmM7efPKjFPYNqPW1evGSIjIpXa8A8Pb05Y-5QW1C-Vok9uZn9T0vxo9N3q-rqvbyvsCz_v_SaNn8JV3QU8foNEznUnUQiSIPYM4M76gEvJHrCUDCZ_88XU9Saz4ECvk2FYXnxemhDSMjZGPw2P6AvDPsr2c_hsAAP__cHOFEg), which was first identified by University of Texas researchers in the 1970s. It was transferred to the paleontology laboratory at Sul Ross and is being studied alongside other vertebrae discovered in the area. [Previous fossil discoveries](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOqzAQRb8GOiN7MA9cuHhNumy7JRrwOIzWsZHtDcnfr4j2D7Y7mpGO7r2f1_mKHDjePvBOtj59miMdJVCtlOfAngrFSnElxzEV_M6Oy5pmkDAIqQXA7JDDa9ats4t0RrVk1aiHXplRmnazXhtn0IyjnyTBJNdpQCMXPelRT6aHlu0pkxpAKan00MkJlR7N6r1Wy4LQaEmOa8pd3ajSE4sPr_Sg3K3p3ga71bqXpv_fwKWBy3Ec3brlFM9vA5ezw3nm4H4Rc-U1nPSWiYVvYqHoRMTKKWIQO-Yv4VMpHARImAZQfbdve5ut2w8Ogcu_sdHydkcO7xT1b9s9LPwEAAD__-CwgzU) from Big Bend National Park include parts of a pterosaur—the largest known flying creature, with an estimated wingspan of 36 feet—and the skull of a horned Bravoceratops, a species only known from Big Bend.

| Friends-
The ultra-wealthy and corporations would have you believe that they make the world turn, but the truth is that the small actions you take every day have a HUGE impact. This Earth Day, here are a few small things you can do to make a big difference.

Winning in Michigan is essential to regaining our Democratic Senate majority, and right now, The Cook Political Report is rating our race as a “toss up.” That means we’re _already_ one of the GOP’s top targets for defeat. Just last year, they spent nearly $80 million trying to buy Michigan’s Senate seat and came up only 0.3% short, so I need your early support to win.

I’m proud to be a lifelong Michigander. I learned the value of hard work by watching my parents – who owned their own landscaping business – build things. Heavy machinery equipment, bobcats, plows, dirt, grease, and grime – it was all part of my childhood.
Later in life, I got the call to give back to the state I love during a time of great uncertainty: the Great Recession. **I can’t tell you how unfathomable it was to hear the words “bankruptcy” and "General Motors" in the same sentence.** So I stepped up to do my part and served as chief of staff for the Auto Rescue initiative under President Obama.
We brought workers, corporations, and union leadership around the same table to stabilize the auto industry. On Friday nights, I’d stay in the office until the late evening to return every call from every Michigander who called worried about the future. _In the end, we saved 200,000 Michigan jobs._
I can’t help but see parallels between then and now as we find ourselves in another moment of great uncertainty, thanks to the chaos forced on us by Donald Trump and his billionaire buddy Elon Musk.
People are rightly concerned about rising costs, shoot-from-the-hip tariffs, and attacks on our personal freedoms. **Michiganders need a fighter in their corner – and that’s who I’ve been my entire life. **

body:
That’s why so many young Americans are choosing despair over hope.

|
