| | [](https://e.updatesforgreatamericans.com/rd/9z2z1nejrumcarj0od05vu3ro53r3lnemi6qara3pk8_rp22sh2s8i6eob5cpj69ob2c5h2bs)
Friend,

The Goldwater Institute is [on a mission to reclaim American history.](https://e.updatesforgreatamericans.com/rd/9z2zpnn9o4qnk34jvgqktvfv349v28dn83u3bbshh7o_rp22sh2s8i6eob5cpj69ob2c5h2bs)

And it starts by getting Marxist propaganda OUT of our schools.

We have only one chance to make that happen, and **we need the help of freedom-loving Americans like you. **

Right now, one in four American public high schools teach history through the lens of one radical socialist: Howard Zinn.

Zinn paints a distorted picture of America, defined by oppression, exploitation, and division. He ignores the values that made America a beacon of freedom and opportunity.

**That 's why our colleges are hotbeds of hate and anti-Americanism. That's why so many young Americans see socialism as the "solution."**

That's why so many young Americans are choosing despair over hope.
[The Goldwater Institute is liberating the minds of American students. Donate now to support our mission >> ](https://e.updatesforgreatamericans.com/rd/9z2z1qspojlescg317n75icq4rfs2g0fqie6qmaub10_rp22sh2s8i6eob5cpj69ob2c5h2bs)
[Donate Now](https://e.updatesforgreatamericans.com/rd/9z2zqtflc6qgn4hfu1e6r8mfbtplbnk14buhtu183j0_rp22sh2s8i6eob5cpj69ob2c5h2bs)
We are exposing this radicalism and giving parents the resources they need to ensure that America's children learn our nation's founding principles.

As a service to parents and educators, the Goldwater Institute's Van Sittert Center for Constitutional Advocacy compared two of the most ambitious and prominent literary projects ever undertaken to teach high schoolers the history of the United States of America: Howard Zinn's _A People 's History of the United States_, and Wilfred McClay's _Land of Hope: An Invitation to the Great American Story_ -- a textbook that gives students an honest, balanced view of both America's virtues and struggles.

Our report details to parents how the adoption of one text versus the other will determine which narrative about the American experiment future generations adopt.

# [Trump's crocodile tears on antisemitism](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=161462508&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTYxNDYyNTA4LCJpYXQiOjE3NDUzMjU0MjAsImV4cCI6MTc0NzkxNzQyMCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.1Dx9v8POqt4i4hVZ40GDNtgHFRN3b-Y04MIa1Df_qqw)
### Trump has made his attack on Harvard all about antisemitism. That's nonsense.
| | [Ben Samuels](https://substack.com/@bensamuels)
---
| Apr 22
---
| [](https://substack.com/@bensamuels)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=161462508&utm_source=substack&isFreemail=true&submitLike=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTYxNDYyNTA4LCJyZWFjdGlvbiI6IuKdpCIsImlhdCI6MTc0NTMyNTQyMCwiZXhwIjoxNzQ3OTE3NDIwLCJpc3MiOiJwdWItMjQ0MDM5OCIsInN1YiI6InJlYWN0aW9uIn0.WJBDJDZ1y6v9Z2vH39PVr4qUuiM7O5_IjHtTKkosDFc&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-reaction&r=1hvr60)
---
| | [](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=161462508&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&isFreemail=true&comments=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTYxNDYyNTA4LCJpYXQiOjE3NDUzMjU0MjAsImV4cCI6MTc0NzkxNzQyMCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.1Dx9v8POqt4i4hVZ40GDNtgHFRN3b-Y04MIa1Df_qqw&r=1hvr60&utm_campaign=email-half-magic-comments&action=post-comment&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=161462508&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTYxNDYyNTA4LCJpYXQiOjE3NDUzMjU0MjAsImV4cCI6MTc0NzkxNzQyMCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.1Dx9v8POqt4i4hVZ40GDNtgHFRN3b-Y04MIa1Df_qqw)
---
| | [](https://substack..KUJA0SzRP1syRp66kqihlFaWUhclWAYtV2s1CfBx7gU?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/bensamuels/p/trumps-crocodile-tears-on-antisemitism?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

In his first 100 days in office, Trump has gone after [political enemies](https://substack.com/redirect/edf8b24a-bf42-4262-b1e5-cadb5b575a73?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [law firms](https://substack.com/redirect/fed10e83-7fb6-434a-8c15-685ad16937f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [universities](https://substack.com/redirect/103b8c4a-2dae-459a-bc07-f8b07d795d07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [the press](https://substack.com/redirect/b2d58cd1-c30f-4ae5-9bdc-31a75093d88b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), threatening anyone who isn't submissive with the full might of the U.S. Presidency. So it was reassuring to see that Harvard [refused to cave to Trump's demands](https://substack.com/redirect/4118404f-ef80-48f9-8c83-83f469c8e3ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
I don't know where this fight ends,1 and I'm not here to comment on the (il)legality or (im)morality of what Trump is doing--plenty of other people are doing that.
What I do want to discuss: nominally, the pretense for this is [Harvard's antisemitism](https://substack.com/redirect/20df7c68-79a7-4b56-8dc4-0528498e4966?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).2 This is nonsense.
* Trump and his administration do not care about antisemitism.
* By using antisemitism as the nominal pretense to exact personal and political revenge, what they're doing is **bad for Jews, bad for the fight against bigotry, and bad for the country.**

I'm Jewish, and [Jewish issues are personal to me](https://substack.com/redirect/5f6282a5-e231-45be-bbf4-0d526a182c25?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). There are real issues with antisemitism and bigotry on college campuses that we need to fight.
**But this fight is about academic freedom, research, and an overreaching executive keen to use the Jews as a political tool.**
[ Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9iZW5zYW11ZWxzLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9hY2NvdW50IiwicCI6MTYxNDYyNTA4LCJzIjoyNDQwMzk4LCJmIjp0cnVlLCJ1Ijo5MDUwMTE5MiwiaWF0IjoxNzQ1MzI1NDIwLCJleHAiOjE3NDc5MTc0MjAsImlzcyI6InB1Yi0wIiwic3ViIjoibGluay1yZWRpcmVjdCJ9.jbuX6iYgMGPsmZm8THf-Uv7s2qsbSKPlGA82wcMVq20?)
> _**Article summary:**_
> * _Antisemitism on college campuses is real, but today 's Republican Party has profound issues with antisemitism in their own ranks that they've never bothered to address. They don't care about actually helping Jews._
> * _Political bias on college campuses is a real challenge too. But Trump 's proposed remedies constitute breathtaking overreach without serious solutions._
> * _Cutting funding for research at these institutions won 't solve antisemitism and won't solve political biases. Funding cuts will, however, hamstring our ability to do life-saving medical research and stunt the growth of future scientists and researchers._
>

### Antisemitism and political bias on college campuses are real problems
We need to be clear about both up front. Democrats and the political left have done a piss-poor job acknowledging that these are two very real issues.
First: there is a very real political bias among university professors.3
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/713fe0a2-72d2-4386-88a5-bbdce289b8aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Relative to the U.S. population, university professors are twice as likely to be liberal, and they're significantly more liberal than even Americans with postgraduate degrees, the country's most liberal demographic (by education). At places like Harvard, the [disconnect is even more stark](https://substack.com/redirect/c82a4bd6-f68d-45a2-a0f4-cb823f2bff51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).4
Second: antisemitism on college campuses is a real problem. Hillel reports that the [number of antisemitic incidents on college campuses is 7× higher](https://substack.com/redirect/2093ebcc-c0b1-44f9-b5ba-97da7694e4a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) than it was before October 7. Dozens of Hillels and Chabad houses have [been threatened, attacked, and vandalized](https://substack.com/redirect/2a5b02d9-8b6f-417d-a6b0-2e88d1e4481b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).5
Columbia's [Task Force on Antisemitism found that](https://substack.com/redirect/2673ea80-7fec-45b4-8a94-fd0de112c1d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "Jewish and Israeli students also have been targeted with violence...and threats." At [Berkeley](https://substack.com/redirect/409683d4-a5d6-4ee8-8514-9c4bee18677b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Harvard](https://substack.com/redirect/49f1b2a0-1937-4bf3-802a-4497e2c91fd5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Temple University](https://substack.com/redirect/91680d78-d690-4831-95f7-57b11aa062e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [University of Texas](https://substack.com/redirect/a87b36bd-2035-4c87-92c9-5919a97933bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [University of Michigan](https://substack.com/redirect/6faf969a-1bcd-417f-9706-0309a2bea430?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [DePaul](https://substack.com/redirect/b102a5bf-ec30-4171-9b2c-458ae3e395d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [University of Rochester](https://substack.com/redirect/9ed07b5d-cf01-44ef-9970-f7d023d4026a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and countless other schools, there have been very real antisemitic incidents.
Like the rest of the country, Jews moved to the right in the 2024 election.6 This is a huge part of the reason why. (Jews still overwhelmingly supported Harris over Trump.)
Republicans, to their credit, saw the political potential here.7 And if they were sincere about addressing academic freedom and antisemitism, I'd be more inclined to support what they say they're trying to do.
The problem is that they're not. **The Trump administration is not sincere about addressing these issues**. They want to assert power, nothing more.
### Trump (and other Republicans) don't care about solving antisemitism
Trump does not care about addressing antisemitism. If he did, he certainly has had a _lot_ of chances to say something in the past:
* There is literally a Wikipedia page titled "[Donald Trump and antisemitism](https://substack.com/redirect/8b10c3bd-070d-4ccd-8361-773c3611c592?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," which is never a great start. ### Trump's demands for Harvard are about asserting control
When it comes to antisemitism, the Trump administration is happy to cut [funding for local Holocaust museums](https://substack.com/redirect/7caa0974-dee8-45fd-aeed-8c48b0ecb350?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) or for [essential security services that keep synagogues](https://substack.com/redirect/cd545701-3abe-4cb6-8ea2-9023487a9f40?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (and other religious congregations) safe.
But for an administration that's nominally about smaller government, they sure want the government involved in a lot of things when it comes to "addressing antisemitism" at Harvard. Non-exhaustively, [here's what's included](https://substack.com/redirect/bae1cab0-d9c0-443b-9dce-ffb0efb1067d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in their list of demands:
* "All hiring and related data shall be shared with the federal government and subjected to a comprehensive audit..."
* "Every department or field found to lack viewpoint diversity must be reformed by hiring a critical mass of new faculty within that department or field who will provide viewpoint diversity..." (No clarity is given for who gets to define this or what specifically this means.)
* Ban certain student groups and "reform its student discipline policies."
* "Harvard must implement a comprehensive mask ban with serious and immediate penalties for violation, not less than suspension."

Harvard, rightly, didn't comply with this sort of insane overreach. And since then, the [Trump administration has pulled funding](https://substack.com/redirect/50bcb9dc-9264-4ce8-bea8-4ecfe2c5d9bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), threatened the University's tax exempt status, threatened the visas of foreign students, and more.
That's not policy-making. That's extortion.
### Real problems, fake solutions
"Find me a moment in history when Jews anywhere benefited from a mix of rampant nationalism and repression. You'll be looking awhile."
That was a quote from a [recent op-ed](https://substack.com/redirect/e0b0e0d3-f3d1-49c0-a411-f8b97113bfa6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). It feels particularly resonant in this context: the federal government is using Jews and antisemitism as a tool to accomplish its political goals. If they really cared about antisemitism, then they're awfully silent when it comes to bigotry in their own ranks.
A few final thoughts on all of this:
1. **We need to address antisemitism in the United States**. These sorts of policies don't advance the cause, but they do politicize an issue that shouldn't be politicized. For all the reasons I outlined above, I cannot trust the Trump administration or today's Republican Party to actually make things better for Jews.
2. Campuses have always leaned left, but in this moment of intense political division, **addressing political bias on college campuses is obviously important**.13 But for the federal government to insist on what students and faculty can and cannot believe is impractical and, more to the point, totally un-American.
3. **All Americans will suffer if we start cutting funding for research** at universities.14

We've made [remarkable gains in public health](https://substack.com/redirect/dee07049-6faf-4e6f-855e-a1ada1af17ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the last 50 years, in no small part because of research support from the federal government. And perhaps even more importantly, we're training the next generation of scientists--Americans by birth or Americans by choice--who lead research in everything from cancer to HIV/AIDS to childhood diseases.
Instead, in the name of political vengeance, we're making it harder for the world's best and brightest to learn and research, and we're slashing funding for causes that improve all of our lives.
What Trump is doing isn't just totally ineffective in addressing antisemitism and political bias. **What he 's doing is bad for economic growth, bad for our health, and bad for the quality of all of our lives.**

* As I've said [once before](https://substack.com/redirect/6ea8cdeb-61b6-4011-bd67-44de4f2c0a7b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), I think [this Yair Rosenberg op-ed](https://substack.com/redirect/d5fbcc55-ee80-49ed-aa95-1876f8b6606d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is spot on: "Trump keeps pushing anti-Semitic stereotypes. But he thinks he's praising Jews."
* More than anything, I think Trump values loyalty and he doesn't care where that comes from. That's why it was so hard for him to condemn the White supremacists protesting in Charlottesville--they were fans of his, and he likes that.
* Trump has Jewish members of his cabinet and Jewish grandchildren. (His daughter Ivanka converted to Judaism before marrying Jared Kushner.) He also has antisemites in his cabinet. Again, I just don't think he cares one way or another, as long as you're loyal.

12
Interestingly enough, the example of crocodile tears [on the Wikipedia page](https://substack.com/redirect/70106471-8022-4ba6-9d3a-e3b1250c626e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is also about antisemitism, this time in the context of Ulysses S. Grant: he claimed to care about the persecution of Russian Jews despite [his own history of antisemitism as a General](https://substack.com/redirect/225c0bcf-ae73-469b-85c6-4fe44a7d07d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) during the Civil War.
13
The "how" here is important and I'll write more about this coming up.
14
Is federal grant money for science research spent particularly efficiently? No, probably not, and there are real ways to make the government work better--[something I've written about before](https://substack.com/redirect/cb2d810c-255a-4c13-ba85-c35a6fdf2f3e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). But we should also be taking swings and pursuing moonshots; universities are pretty well positioned to be doing that, in a [partnership with the federal government](https://substack.com/redirect/7ee2bb25-547d-40bc-8faa-484496e4e5b3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that's become more robust over the past few decades.

Substack is a great platform not just because it allows independent writers the ability to build something for themselves, but it also allows those same writers to be honest with how they really feel. However, their honesty can sometimes come back to haunt them in the real world.
The most recent example of this is that of Nicholas Decker. A George Mason PhD student, Decker recently **[wrote on his Substack](https://substack.com/redirect/d423816e-545a-4417-a220-276e4f3f1875?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** asking his fellow leftists when is it enough to start killing members and supporters of the Trump administration.

Decker, while seemingly gleeful at the prospect, frames his desires with apparent reluctance:
"Evil has come to America. The present administration is engaged in barbarism...If the present administration chooses this course, then the questions of the day can be settled not with legislation, but with blood and iron. In short, we must decide when we must kill them. None of us wish for war, but if the present administration wishes to destroy the nation I would accept war rather than see it perish. I hope that you would choose the same."
Decker made it abundantly clear his desire to kill the MAGA movement goes beyond taking out President Donald Trump:
"The rot of the present administration runs deeper than one man. The sacrifice of a hero is insufficient to save our nation, and a gust of wind on a summer day would not have saved us. Medical elites simply don't want **[this secret](https://substack.com/redirect/aafd6eda-ab60-46fb-89c6-9b00e2de273c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as a matter of public record. In the time since his piece went up, it gained almost 400 likes and over 800 comments, most of them are negative.
Decker put an update on the piece in response to the backlash: "Violence is a last resort, not a first resort. It must come after the exhaustion of all possible remedy. It is not, moreover, appropriate for decisions which are merely unwise or disastrous."
Given the nature of the call for violence and far-leftists have carried out acts of terrorism since Trump has been in office, it looks as though **[the Secret Service](https://substack.com/redirect/5da1440e-3560-46df-a134-44898f9bfe30?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** paid Decker a visit. Decker claimed at the end of the visit, it was determined that his conduct was "fully legal."

That's right, even though he posted his desire to kill people he disagrees with politically, making it known he is a danger to others, it is the "internet lunatics" who are to blame for no longer having a place to stay.
Another example showing he has no qualms about his position is by reposting an online mutual who supportively says, "The Secret Service agent asks him if it came down to it, would you participate in any revolution, and he just straight up goes: 'I hope I would have the courage to do so.'"

While he might let other people do what he asks for if things went kinetic, it's the fact he feels comfortable enough to voice it and has gained fans since then are the warning signs all conservatives must heed. Remember, the piece has nearly reached 400 likes.
Like I said, there have been multiple attacks across the country committed by deranged leftists in recent months. It does not take a whole army to cause chaos and mayhem, like the BLM riots in 2020. It does not even have to take 10 people. A singular deranged person can cause a lot of death and damage.
So after mocking such leftists, it is best to not let your guard down. We are in uncharted territory with people who have truly lost their minds.

| [ **JOIN MY WINNING TEAM** ](http://links.tubervilleforalabama.com/u/click?_t=b8b4efbe79f64b579dfa7d8da685a7a9&_m=5da061a4a217448c9ecc7804dcd50fa7&_e=rika6JXp5F0pbBnA-J9E5gVSmgmg8ZEYU1qv1zyEpyQI0Rqw4SuKQpXxWSi8Ixy2lirkSojyjNlygA0Sb8leMehgZrsLkdtHwss8kWBPjH7c3vq-cRO-7hhh32uUblEfVxTXbJIosvrJvdRXLxb7Qv1Tn0p8OtnETrABTaTvfnUEizXjbbyz0VhJJGHttW7mqd5a3eYw3ZiOBPqHkhLABbBrjwEPNG6L85soJDbxvsmR_5ycYS9s41kG_st41ZtTNNTFY3aNu7N98iw7kppx2RX2Od3J2HBP3OSlTQpDAvx7DYXuve34fqsS1Ud34peAeReivLcs0aM6R-h5iPpiOw%3D%3D)

Now, my opponent, a former Republican who supported Democrats at the DNC and shared their hatred for President Trump, thinks that my neighbors in Alabama will turn on me. I’ve got news for him. It won’t happen.

[ **SUPPORT AMERICA-FIRST** ](http://links.tubervilleforalabama.com/u/click?_t=b8b4efbe79f64b579dfa7d8da685a7a9&_m=5da061a4a217448c9ecc7804dcd50fa7&_e=rika6JXp5F0pbBnA-J9E5gVSmgmg8ZEYU1qv1zyEpyQI0Rqw4SuKQpXxWSi8Ixy2lirkSojyjNlygA0Sb8leMehgZrsLkdtHwss8kWBPjH7c3vq-cRO-7hhh32uUblEfVxTXbJIosvrJvdRXLxb7Qv1Tn0p8OtnETrABTaTvfnUEizXjbbyz0VhJJGHttW7mYbX8UXApTmc1dML1J9VoOTMBKfQKaDyWTgdUnV4Zw76O7YjkI9pTCkP7HZc5Qb7zDh4l3RSriEcETkcxk4pdrlFM3wVs9ZJjbXoYzyKJcAT79rtrYVittfmh-X4LGsbfUOFl4uQ10k1sW6H7Fptj-A%3D%3D)

We’re living in President Trump’s America, who won last November’s election in an overwhelming victory. I’m confident that Alabamians will stand with their Senator who’s been by President Trump’s side since DAY ONE.

[**Now, I’m fixing to prove something. I’m asking my TOP SUPPORTERS to officially endorse me in this race. Will you join my America-First Team?**](http://links.tubervilleforalabama.com/u/click?_t=b8b4efbe79f64b579dfa7d8da685a7a9&_m=5da061a4a217448c9ecc7804dcd50fa7&_e=rika6JXp5F0pbBnA-J9E5gVSmgmg8ZEYU1qv1zyEpyQI0Rqw4SuKQpXxWSi8Ixy2lirkSojyjNlygA0Sb8leMehgZrsLkdtHwss8kWBPjH7c3vq-cRO-7hhh32uUblEfVxTXbJIosvrJvdRXLxb7Qv1Tn0p8OtnETrABTaTvfnUEizXjbbyz0VhJJGHttW7mf4015UGMyLe1-zhwGjSGEyE8-IXSkIfEUmV82UnC6F2augfkraey19pBPuI_JU8-3kKBgpDdXQMcSUQXMoqrhD9CgGdMPxUqhA1yBc6pXLtEMWqxgjsPmy9zjarhSt4KEUUeBt2c89hieIzHBWkL2w%3D%3D)

body:
Polis Vetoes Open Records Bill—But Conservatives Say It’s Too Little, Too Late
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi folks,
Listen to today's **Mountain Minute Podcast** [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)! Here is a summary of today's top stories:
**🏛️ Colorado Legislative Session Updates...** Governor Polis vetoed SB25-077, a bill critics say would’ve made public records access a “pay-to-play” system. While he cited concerns about bureaucratic overreach, conservatives say [it’s too little, too late](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Meanwhile, local mom Erin Lee warns HB25-1312 would have labeled her as a child abuser for not affirming her daughters’ [brief gender confusion](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)—raising alarms over constitutional rights and parental freedom.
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** Denver’s [permitting delays](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) are driving up housing costs by as much as $125,000, with builder Robert Treta calling for urgent reform to cut red tape and speed approvals. Meanwhile, two of Colorado’s reintroduced wolves were killed after [crossing into Wyoming](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), where protections are weaker. Dozens of international students are suing after the Trump administration [revoked their visa status](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) over law enforcement interactions.

Lastly, after years of decline, Christian affiliation is stabilizing. Woodmen Valley Chapel just opened a new downtown campus in Colorado Springs on Easter, symbolizing a [rebirth of public faith](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).

🇺🇸 **On the National Stage...** In a seismic moment for the Catholic Church, [Pope Francis has died](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) at age 88. His death comes just one day after meeting with U.S. Vice President JD Vance.

🗣️ **Commentary Spotlight...** Dr. Brian Joondeph argues Democrats are [alienating voters](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) by defending criminal illegal aliens and ignoring victims like Rachel Morin—unpopular stances that could cost them the 2026 midterms as Trump’s approval surges.
This is the Mountain Minute for Tuesday, April 22, 2025.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Polis Vetoes Open Records Bill—But Conservatives Say It’s Too Little, Too Late](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY RMV EDITORIAL BOARD, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Governor Jared Polis vetoed a controversial bill last Thursday that would have made it more difficult—and more expensive—for Coloradans to access public records (Senate Bill 25-077). But transparency advocates across the political spectrum say his sudden concern about responsive governance contradicts years of actions that have consistently chipped away at public accountability.
Polis vetoed the bill on April 17, stating it placed too much discretion in the hands of unelected bureaucrats and could erode equal access to public information.
“Speed to access public information is determined by who you are,” he wrote in his veto letter. “As a representative for the people of Colorado, I support more, not less, openness and transparency.”
But critics are calling out the governor’s convenient shift in tone.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---

The only way we can continue to spread truth is with your support!
[DONATE TO ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
|
---
**[Treta: Denver’s broken permitting system is driving up housing costs—and it’s time to fix it](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Denver’s average permit wait time has ballooned to 385 days, adding roughly $125,000 to the cost of a new home—costs that are passed directly to buyers and renters.
* Although structural designs are already reviewed by licensed engineers, the city still requires full plan reviews, leading to bloated staffing and longer delays without added safety benefits.
* Proposals include eliminating redundant reviews, focusing city staff on quick zoning checks, and restoring one-day permit approvals to cut costs and improve housing affordability.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Colorado’s wolf plan ignores the one thing wolves don’t: borders](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [THE FENCE POST](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Colorado wolves are protected under both state and federal law, but once they cross into Wyoming—where protections were removed in 2017—they can be killed without a license under predator control laws.
* One was taken out by federal Wildlife Services after a livestock incident; another's death remains undisclosed due to Wyoming’s secrecy laws, which shield hunter identities.
* Wolves that enter Utah, Arizona, or New Mexico can be captured and returned under existing agreements. No such pact exists with Wyoming, creating a dangerous gap in management for Colorado’s reintroduced population.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Lee and Friday: We saved our daughters—HB25-1312 would’ve punished us as child abusers](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [WALL STREET JOURNAL](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_We are both mothers whose daughters went through a phase in which they believed they were boys. We never affirmed that belief, although their schools and much of the broader culture did. Eventually, our daughters recognized their true identities and ceased identifying themselves as “transgender.”_
_A bill under consideration in Colorado (where Ms. Lee lives) would define parents like us as child abusers._
_The measure would harm vulnerable children and violate the U.S. Constitution in multiple ways._
_Lawmakers including state Reps. Yara Zokaie and Javier Mabrey have likened parents like us to Klansmen, and their legislation is expected to pass the state Senate and proceed to Gov. Jared Polis’s desk._
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
** ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ **
**[Home Rule Charter Commission candidates must file by April 24 in Douglas County](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY JEN SCHUMANN****| LOCAL | APRIL 18** _Writing the rules that will shape Douglas County’s future might sound like a job you’d rely on lawmakers to handle. But in this case, it could be your neighbor, your coworker – or you._
**[“Boomers at heart,” Gen Z and Gays Against Groomers: Adams Co. GOP kickoff focuses on unity, youth and shared mission](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY RMV NE CO NEWSROOM | LOCAL | APRIL 18** _The Adams County Republican Party held its first general meeting under newly elected leadership on April 17 at the Crossroads Community Center in Northglenn. Approximately 50 attendees gathered to hear updates from party officials, engage in discussions on party involvement, and hear from guest speakers on youth engagement and legislative advocacy._
**[Pastor Drake: Resurrection is the call to become fully alive, fully human–and spiritually reborn](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | APRIL 18** _Easter isn’t just a day we remember—it’s the day that redefined reality. The cross? It wasn’t the end. It was the narrow gate. The resurrection? Not an escape plan—it’s an invitation to walk a different kind of road._

Kennedy were Catholic, most others have been Protestant—particularly Episcopalian or Presbyterian. Thomas Jefferson and Abraham Lincoln held no formal religious affiliation, but no president has openly practiced a religion outside of Christianity.

If you've spent time online lately, you've probably heard from the self-proclaimed defenders of civilization -- the Elon Musks and JD Vances of the world -- who believe the solution to America's declining birthrate is... having more babies.
They've dubbed themselves _pronatalists_ , and they're sounding the alarm: Civilization will collapse, they say, if we don't increase the number of children born in the United States. They propose baby bonuses, fertility education, even reshuffling transportation funding to favor towns with high birth and marriage rates. Some are reportedly pushing the White House to act fast -- as if birthing more humans is a patriotic duty.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/21870cdb-e13d-424c-9832-e95ab6256cc2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Photo by Aly Niklas
But here's the part they never say out loud: it's not really about saving the species. It's about control.
Let's be clear -- choosing to have a child is one of the most personal, vulnerable, and high-stakes decisions a person can make. It involves physical risk, emotional labor, and lifelong financial commitment.
I haven't had children yet, but a few years ago, my partner and I decided to freeze eggs and embryos. It was empowering, but also painful, expensive, and exhausting. I injected myself with hormones, had repeated ultrasounds, took time off training, and landed in the ER with ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome. And that was just to _preserve_ the possibility of future parenthood. I know it pales in comparison to what so many women experience through pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum, and parenting -- but it gave me a glimpse into the strength and sacrifice it takes to build a family in today's world.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1fee6f34-2382-484a-9d35-8273bbc722fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Now imagine doing that in a country that barely supports pregnant people, where Roe v. Wade has been overturned, where IVF is under legal threat, and where women are being criminalized for miscarriage. That's the America today's pronatalists have helped create.
You can't claim to care about birthrates while stripping people of their reproductive freedom.
And you can't ignore the real economic conditions driving people away from parenthood. If Elon Musk and his allies were serious about helping families, they'd be fighting for:
* **Universal paid parental leave**
* **Affordable childcare and universal pre-K**
* **Postpartum mental health and pelvic floor care**
* **Legal protection for IVF, contraception, and abortion access**
* **Wages that actually keep up with the cost of living**
* **Affordable housing in safe, healthy communities**
* **Common sense gun laws** , so parents don't fear sending their kids to school -- and kids aren't traumatized by active shooter drills
* **Climate action and clean air/water protections** , so children aren't growing up with asthma, poisoned drinking water, or a planet that's too hot to survive
* **Strong, independent public health agencies like the CDC and FDA** , so we can trust our vaccines, prevent outbreaks of diseases like measles, and keep our food and medicine safe

Instead, we get dystopian tweets, fertility propaganda, and billionaires like Elon Musk -- who, according to _The Wall Street Journal_ , has fathered at least 14 children with multiple women and is building a private compound in Texas to house his "legion" of offspring -- while the rest of us can't even find an OB-GYN taking new patients.
I've been told online that I "work better as a ho than a senator," that I should "go back to making sandwiches," and that I "look breedable." These aren't isolated comments -- they're part of a loud, coordinated movement to take us backward.
But we're not going back.
We won't go back to a time when women's roles were limited to birthing and obedience. We won't go back to policies that ignore the realities of modern parenthood and environmental collapse. We won't go back to lawmakers criminalizing fertility care while ignoring the daily crises that families face.
Because being _truly_ pro-life means supporting **quality of life**. Not punishing women. Not forcing birth in a healthcare desert. Not sacrificing our kids to gun violence, polluted air, or preventable diseases.
As someone who's climbed the world's highest mountains -- and fought for equality every step of the way -- I can tell you this: building a just, compassionate society is a lot harder than building a family compound in Texas.
If you're with me, join the movement. Subscribe, share this with a friend and if you're a free subscriber, consider upgrading to paid. Let's build a future where every person has the freedom to decide if, when, and how to have a family. And the support they need no matter what they choose.

## Hamas & hate at Coachella

Dear Neighbors,

On July 31, 2024, resident Mose James IV took the rare step of filing a recall petition to remove Councilwoman Jamelle McKenzie.[

Many neighbors](https://exeprx.clicks.mlsend.com/tl/c/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjEwNTM2NTUsXCJsXCI6MTUyMzg2MjUxNTM5ODc1Njk0LFwiclwiOjE1MjM4NjMwMTUwODcxNjA5M30iLCJzIjoiOTA5NjkxNmIyNmU4NmIzZCJ9) from Ward One joined the effort, concerned about the direction our city was heading under their newly elected councilperson.

The issues were real—and they still are:
* A proposed **[battery plant](https://exeprx.clicks.mlsend.com/tl/c/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjEwNTM2NTUsXCJsXCI6MTUyMzg2MjUxNTQ1MTE4NTc2LFwiclwiOjE1MjM4NjMwMTUwODcxNjA5M30iLCJzIjoiYTVkZDM5NWZhZTU3NTZhMSJ9)** just steps from homes
* The **[sale of Bill Evans Field](https://exeprx.clicks.mlsend.com/tl/c/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjEwNTM2NTUsXCJsXCI6MTUyMzg2MjUxNTUwMzYxNDU4LFwiclwiOjE1MjM4NjMwMTUwODcxNjA5M30iLCJzIjoiYzQ3NmEwNTRhMzUwODZlYiJ9)**
* **Low morale and high turnover** among city staff
* A council vote to **limit transparency** by [silencing the mayor](https://exeprx.clicks.mlsend.com/tl/c/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjEwNTM2NTUsXCJsXCI6MTUyMzg2MjUxNTU0NTU1NzY2LFwiclwiOjE1MjM4NjMwMTUwODcxNjA5M30iLCJzIjoiN2NjNWI0MzY0ZjQ0OTk4NSJ9)
* And a growing pattern of **ignoring residents’ voices**

This movement was never about politics. It was—and still is—about people. **People who care enough to ask hard questions, stand up for each other, and demand better from those in power.** We’re proud of what we’ve done together, and we remain committed to building the College Park we all deserve. But after much reflection, [we’ve made the tough decision to move past the recall effort](https://exeprx.clicks.mlsend.com/tl/c/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjEwNTM2NTUsXCJsXCI6MTUyMzg2MjUxNTYxODk1Nzk5LFwiclwiOjE1MjM4NjMwMTUwODcxNjA5M30iLCJzIjoiNGRjZTRjMDk1MTdmZjZhOCJ9). The truth is: while the city spent over **$122,000** of your tax dollars fighting this recall in court (just from August through December—we still don’t know how much more has been spent since), our team relied entirely on **volunteers**. Neighbors who donated their time, energy, and legal expertise to fight for something better. But we cannot continue down a path where the city uses **our own money against us** , while we exhaust ourselves trying to hold them accountable. So instead, we’re shifting our focus to the issues that still demand our attention:
* **Stopping the battery plant**
* **Expanding access to healthcare** in our community
* **Holding city leaders accountable** for big promises, like the still-**Six West development**

We stand committed to the ideals we set out for last July. This is **doubling down on the future of College Park**. We want to extend a heartfelt thank you to our lead counsel, **James Walker** , whose expertise and dedication guided us through this process. He was supported by **Elizabeth Lester** , **Sherry Godfrey** , **Tom Coleman** , and many others who lent their time, voice, and heart—because they, too, want the best for College Park.
Thank you for standing with us. Thank you for believing. Let’s keep building—together.

In Mississippi, the relationship between doctors and nurse practitioners (NPs) tries to blends collaboration with strict oversight. This dynamic is an attempt to address Mississippi's physician shortage while sparking debate over autonomy and care quality. Comparing it to neighboring states like Arkansas highlights unique challenges and opportunities in this physician-led partnership.
**Legal Framework: Reduced Practice**
Mississippi's "reduced practice" model requires NPs to have a collaborative agreement with a doctor to practice and prescribe. Overseen by the Mississippi Board of Nursing and Medical Licensure, this mandates monthly chart reviews (10% or 20 charts) by the physician, who can be 75 miles away if using electronic records and meeting practice-hour minimums (20 hours weekly or 80 monthly). This contrasts with Arkansas, which also requires collaboration but allows NPs to own practices and has fewer geographic limits, offering more flexibility.
**Daily Collaboration**
NPs, with advanced nursing degrees, manage routine care--checkups, chronic conditions, minor issues--while relying on doctors, with their 10,000+ clinical hours, for complex cases. In Mississippi's primary-care-starved rural clinics, NPs are often the main providers, consulting doctors remotely. Arkansas NPs enjoy similar teamwork but face less rigid oversight, enabling faster responses to patient needs without as much red tape.
**Tensions and Regional Differences**
The collaboration mandate stirs controversy. NPs argue it hampers their ability to serve Mississippi's 91% underserved counties, where the physician ratio is a nation-low 184.7 per 100,000. Studies show NPs match doctors in primary care safety, yet Mississippi clings to oversight. Doctors, citing their extensive training, defend it as a quality safeguard, pointing to higher costs under non-physician care in some studies. Arkansas, while collaborative, leans toward NP autonomy, easing practice setup compared to Mississippi's tighter leash. Full-practice states like Tennessee and Louisiana go further, ditching collaboration entirely, a model NPs here covet but lawmakers reject--2024 bills like SB 2079 failed again.
**Healthcare Impact**
With 3,500 NPs and 5,500 doctors (1,900 in primary care), Mississippi relies on this partnership to stretch resources. NPs run rural clinics under distant supervision, offering vital care where hospitals have closed. Yet, losing a collaborating doctor disrupts service, unlike Arkansas, where NPs can pivot more easily. Patients get hybrid care--NPs as the frontline, doctors as backup--but the system's fragility shows in Mississippi's stricter rules versus Arkansas's looser reins.
**Conclusion**
Mississippi's doctor-NP relationship tries to balance teamwork with control, unlike Arkansas's more permissive approach or Tennessee's full NP freedom. As of April 2025, it fills gaps in a state with dire shortages but fuels debate over whether oversight aids or hinders care. Aligning with regional trends could ease access, yet Mississippi holds fast, making this partnership both a lifeline and a point of contention.

name: Sen. Jon Ossoff
subject: My decision
body:
Let me lay this out, clear as day:

[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-ossoff-dnc?refcode=em250422&refcode2=526_2563979_w82pZ9&akid=526%2E2563979%2Ew82pZ9)
---
Let me lay this out, clear as day:
I am the only Democratic Senator up for re-election in a state Trump won in 2024.
And the President said he’ll back Marjorie Taylor Greene to challenge me.
This Senate race in Georgia will be the most competitive and most expensive in the nation.
If you’re outraged by what’s happening to our country — and you’re ready to fight -- please rush $5 to my re-election campaign and the Democratic National Committee today.
Here’s the link to donate:[**https://act.kamalaharris.com/go/defend-Jon](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-ossoff-dnc?refcode=em250422&refcode2=526_2563979_w82pZ9&akid=526%2E2563979%2Ew82pZ9)**
Otherwise, let me remind you why I ran for Senate — and why this moment is just as urgent.
Before I was elected, I led investigations of corruption and human rights abuses worldwide. We exposed wrongdoing in countries where criticizing the government is dangerous, where whistleblowers and witnesses will only meet in secret, where protest carries the risk of prosecution.
More and more, the atmosphere under Trump reminded me of those places where dissent was silenced by intimidation.
Trump’s rise wasn’t just a crisis. It was a warning.
I ran for Senate because I saw the danger in electing someone so profoundly unfit for the presidency and I wanted to confront the corruption that made his rise possible.
I also ran -- years before the Dobbs decision -- because it was already clear the GOP was coming for reproductive rights. I saw Georgia as the front line in that fight. With a six-week ban now in place here, and Republicans pushing for a national abortion ban, it still is.
Now this President is staging a power grab unprecedented in our history. In his first 100 days:
* He’s freed violent criminals who attacked the Capitol on his behalf.
* Purged independent watchdogs across government.
* Stacked key agencies with loyalists—and called on them to investigate his political opponents.
* Defied and threatened federal judges.
* Undermined the press.
* Handed sweeping, unaccountable power to the billionaire who spent $300 million to elect him.

Trump’s goal isn’t just revenge. He wants to use the government to crush the opposition. And now, Americans are living in fear of their own government.
This is not a drill and it’s not a bad dream. As citizens, it is the test of our lifetimes.
In 2020, the pundits said flipping a Republican Senate seat in Georgia couldn’t be done. But we built one of the strongest voter mobilization programs in Senate campaign history—and we won. That victory won the Senate majority.
Now we must win again. And we will win again.
Just like last time, I can’t do it alone.
So I’m asking:
[**Please make a contribution to my re-election campaign and the Democratic National Committee today of $5 or any amount that works for you.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-ossoff-dnc?refcode=em250422&refcode2=526_2563979_w82pZ9&akid=526%2E2563979%2Ew82pZ9)
The average online donation to our campaign is around $30. Many give less. Some give more.
All that matters is that lots and lots of people are contributing what they can to power our grassroots campaign. Please, contribute today.
**[DONATE](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-ossoff-dnc?refcode=em250422&refcode2=526_2563979_w82pZ9&akid=526%2E2563979%2Ew82pZ9)**
Thanks for being part of this team.
As always,
Jon Ossoff

This email was sent to **dpwillis67@gmail.com**. Thank you so much for being a supporter. But we don't want to bother you. If you’d like to unsubscribe, you can **[click here.](https://harris.actionkit.com/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe?t=1&akid=526%2E2563979%2Ew82pZ9)**

body:
I’ll tell you – the future is bright for the MAGA movement!

[](https://e.realamericanreporting.com/rd/9z2za3k853o8188rpjvj364r130r2rl1alrvkvq975o_rp22sh2s8i6eob5cpgmcp72cdh2bs)Hi, it's Charlie Kirk.
I'll tell you - the future is bright for the MAGA movement!
I knew young folks were breaking for the GOP even before Election Day. I could feel it in my bones. The sheer number of college students turning out for our events was inspiring.
Young men and women rejected the Joe Biden/Kamala Harris regime defined by rising prices, open borders, expensive housing, and blatant government waste funded by our tax dollars.
Now a new generation of Conservatives - inspired by our President - are rising up to meet this moment, including JD Vance, Donald Trump Jr., Republican influencers, Members of Congress, and MAGA candidates running in big races.
**One of those candidates is my friend, Vivek Ramaswamy. **[](https://e.realamericanreporting.com/rd/9z2zcs779fg6fhk65avb2h10tqdt8adkmhcbvga2a50_rp22sh2s8i6eob5cpgmcp72cdh2bs)When Vivek told me he was running for Governor of Ohio, I was thrilled. I quickly invited him on my show to talk about why he's running and discuss how he'd work with the President.
He didn't disappoint.
Vivek talked about expanding our Party by slashing the state income tax, expanding school choice, cutting back property taxes, strengthening American energy, and bringing the heartland roaring back.
Young voters will love this platform. Our seniors will love this platform. Ohioans will love this platform. And anyone outside of Ohio will push for this platform in their own states.
Mark my words - Vivek's campaign promises will pop up in every major race this coming cycle.
[And you get to be a part of it from the very beginning.](https://e.realamericanreporting.com/rd/9z2zcgok465bcv8bm8s5pog9s9o47jf6umsr9u494og_rp22sh2s8i6eob5cpgmcp72cdh2bs)** That's why I'm personally asking you to support Vivek Ramaswamy's campaign today. It can be $4 or $400 - it doesn't matter how much you give. **
All that matters is that everyone reading this pitches in something.

body:
Friend,

On Election Day this November 2025, I don't just want to win — I want to win big.
Because as Democrats, the bigger we win in Virginia in 2025, the louder a message we'll send about the 2026 midterms.
People in Virginia and across the country are looking at our race as a bellwether for Democrats. In every zip code and every community, Democrats are understandably frightened and angry about the chaos coming out of Washington. And to them, our race is a beacon of hope. It’s an opportunity to chart the path out of this dark chapter in our nation’s history.
And can I be honest for a minute? That's a lot of weight on my shoulders. But I'm ready to seize the moment and win big. I feel honored that people have put so much hope into our campaign, and it’s a big reason why I've worked to stay above the fray and focus on what matters: winning big and delivering real, meaningful change when we do.
And I hope that as you read this email, you’ll buy into that vision too. Because there is light at the end of the tunnel. We just have to keep going. So let's win big in 2025 — so we can win big in 2026, and 2027, and 2028, and beyond.

The Virginia Governor’s race isn’t just about the future of Virginia

Peter,
I’ve seen a lot of tough races in my time, but let me tell you: **this one is as important as it gets.**
The Virginia Governor’s race isn’t just about the future of Virginia – it's a bellwether for the entire country. This will be the first major election after Trump’s inauguration, and it could set the stage for Democrats in 2026. If we don’t win big here, we’ll be facing a rough road ahead.
**[So, before I continue, can I count on you to split a contribution between Abigail Spanberger’s campaign for Governor of Virginia and Heartland Patriots?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/87995?refcode=em20250422-8890&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=8890%2E614464%2EVZ8sKe)**

Here’s what’s got me terrified:
The _Cook Political Report_ has called this race a TOSS-UP, and I couldn’t agree more. Polls are going to stay tight, and this race is going to be one of the hardest-fought in the nation. Republicans are going to flood the state with millions of dollars through their super PACs, trying to keep the Governor’s seat red. They know this race is everything to them – and we need to match their energy, their money, and their commitment. Remember, this race is the only opportunity to flip a Governor's office from red to blue in 2025.
If we don’t win this one, we’ll be handing Republicans a major victory ahead of 2026, and trust me – we can’t let that happen.
Right now, Democratic Governors are our last line of defense against the reckless policies coming out of the Trump administration, and Abigail Spanberger is the leader Virginia needs at this moment.
That’s why I’m asking you to step up today. We can’t win this without your help. The money that’s coming from the other side is going to be massive, and we need to be able to push back. Her message is below:_ [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106288758/541031640/-88581091?amount=10&refcode=em_sp_2025.04.22_b1_hs_all&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85NTEyNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4NzA3ODU1MS04YTFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Wj62MXWsrXonpfHrskTGOb25Dz1AgGyCXxFH6yZqjfg=) Hi, Peter – this is Congresswoman Haley Stevens writing to you with exciting news: Today, I’m launching my campaign for Michigan’s open U.S. Senate seat. I’m proud to be a lifelong Michigander. I learned the value of hard work by watching my parents – who owned their own landscaping business – build things. Heavy machinery equipment, bobcats, plows, dirt, grease, and grime – it was all part of my childhood.
Later in life, I got the call to give back to the state I love during a time of great uncertainty: the Great Recession. **I can’t tell you how unfathomable it was to hear the words “bankruptcy” and “General Motors” in the same sentence.** So I stepped up to do my part and served as chief of staff for the Auto Rescue initiative under President Obama.
We brought workers, corporations, and union leadership around the same table to stabilize the auto industry. On Friday nights, I’d stay in the office until the late evening and return every call from every Michigander who called our office worried about the future. _In the end, we saved 200,000 Michigan jobs._
I can’t help but see parallels between then and now as we find ourselves in another moment of great uncertainty, thanks to the chaos forced on us by Donald Trump and his billionaire buddy Elon Musk.
People are rightly concerned about rising costs, shoot-from-the-hip tariffs, and attacks on our personal freedoms. **Michiganders need a fighter in their corner – and that’s who I’ve been my entire life.**

Her message is below: = Hi, Peter – this is Congresswoman Haley Stevens writing to you with exciting news: Today, I’m launching my campaign for Michigan’s open U.S. Senate seat. Winning in Michigan is essential to regaining our Democratic Senate majority, and right now The Cook Political Report is rating our race as a “Toss Up.” That means we’re already one of the GOP’s top targets for defeat. Just last year, they spent nearly $80 million trying to buy Michigan’s Senate seat and came up only 0.3% short, so I need your early support to win. Peter, I want to tell you a bit more about myself and why I’m running.= | = I’m proud to be a lifelong Michigander. I learned the value of hard work by watching my parents – who owned their own landscaping business – build things. Heavy machinery equipment, bobcats, plows, dirt, grease, and grime – it was all part of my childhood. Later in life, I got the call to give back to the state I love during a time of great uncertainty: the Great Recession. I can’t tell you how unfathomable it was to hear the words “bankruptcy” and “General Motors” in the same sentence. So I stepped up to do my part and served as chief of staff for the Auto Rescue initiative under President Obama. We brought workers, corporations, and union leadership around the same table to stabilize the auto industry. On Friday nights, I’d stay in the office until the late evening and return every call from every Michigander who called our office worried about the future. In the end, we saved 200,000 Michigan jobs. confirmed member of the vicious MS-13 international terrorist gang.

Voter Action Project
Folks -- Every eligible American deserves the freedom to vote without jumping through impossible hoops.
The SAVE Act would scare newly naturalized citizens out of voting and make it harder for millions of eligible voters to cast a ballot – especially seniors, women, students, veterans, and rural voters.
The House of Representatives has passed the SAVE Act – a cruel, calculated attack on every American’s right to vote. The Senate must REJECT the anti-voter SAVE Act and protect our right to vote.
We’ve all seen what happens when voting rights are stripped away. People lose their voice, communities lose power, and elections no longer belong to We The People – they belong to those who make the rules.
Add your name to our petition urging the Senate to REJECT the SAVE Act >> [https://act.commoncause.org/petitions/tell-the-senate-reject-the-anti-voter-save-act-2?source=041625swap-ifvap&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.everyaction.com%2F9bivrSvjFEim0QMMvgcQrA2]
SIGN HERE NOW ⇨ [https://act.commoncause.org/petitions/tell-the-senate-reject-the-anti-voter-save-act-2?source=041625swap-ifvap&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.everyaction.com%2F9bivrSvjFEim0QMMvgcQrA2]
It’s designed to effectively block millions of eligible Americans from casting a ballot – especially women, seniors, students, and rural voters.
Here’s how the “SAVE” Act puts your vote at risk: [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/save-the-usps-3/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.everyaction.com%2F9bivrSvjFEim0QMMvgcQrA2]
* Prove your citizenship – again: Even if you’re a lifelong voter, if you move across town, change your last name when getting married, or switch parties, you’d have to provide your passport or birth certificate with your current legal name – in person at your local elections office – just to stay registered.
* Get stuck in long lines: Election officials would face impossible workloads, causing confusion and delays.
* Lose your right to vote – without warning: If outdated records can’t verify your status, you could be purged from the rolls without even knowing it.
We still have time to pressure the Senate to stop this – but only if we speak out NOW.
Let’s show the Senate just how many of us are paying attention and demanding they protect our freedom to vote. Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. The SAVE Act would scare newly naturalized citizens out of voting and make it harder for millions of eligible voters to cast a ballot – especially seniors, women, students, veterans, and rural voters. The House of Representatives has passed the SAVE Act – a cruel, calculated attack on every American’s right to vote. The Senate must REJECT the anti-voter SAVE Act and protect our right to vote. We’ve all seen what happens when voting rights are stripped away. People lose their voice, communities lose power, and elections no longer belong to We The People – they belong to those who make the rules. Add your name to our petition urging the Senate to REJECT the SAVE Act >> [] SIGN HERE NOW ⇨ [] It’s designed to effectively block millions of eligible Americans from casting a ballot – especially women, seniors, students, and rural voters. Here’s how the “SAVE” Act puts your vote at risk: [] Prove your citizenship – again: Even if you’re a lifelong voter, if you move across town, change your last name when getting married, or switch parties, you’d have to provide your passport or birth certificate with your current legal name – in person at your local elections office – just to stay registered. Get stuck in long lines: Election officials would face impossible workloads, causing confusion and delays. * Lose your right to vote – without warning: If outdated records can’t verify your status, you could be purged from the rolls without even knowing it. We still have time to pressure the Senate to stop this – but only if we speak out NOW. Let’s show the Senate just how many of us are paying attention and demanding they protect our freedom to vote. 1. Ensure access to clean air and clean water. As a co-chair on the Chesapeake Bay Watershed Taskforce, I’m continuing my work to protect and preserve the Bay for generations to come.
2. Combat the climate crisis. As the Trump Administration tries to roll back critical environmental protections, I’m not giving up the fight. That's why I’ve joined over 100 of my Democratic colleagues in urging Speaker Johnson to take action on the climate crisis.
3. Fight against invasive species. I’m happy to share that I introduced the first – and only – Democratic amendment to pass the House Committee on Natural Resources, which protects the Chesapeake Bay from invasive aquatic species.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106293107/541045056/-1222209541?refcode=email_042225_deluziostevens&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjU0MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmZDQ4NzZhMy04ZTFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Sjaaz-kp3OirTfFIQwIbfcnzmQddgK81LBhfMjPNobQ=) Hi, Derek – this is Congresswoman Haley Stevens writing to you with exciting news: Today, I’m launching my campaign for Michigan’s open U.S. Senate seat. Winning in Michigan is essential to regaining our Democratic Senate majority, and right now The Cook Political Report is rating our race as a “Toss Up.” That means we’re _already_ one of the GOP’s top targets for defeat. Just last year, they spent nearly $80 million trying to buy Michigan’s Senate seat and came up only 0.3% short, so I need your early support to win. **Derek, I want to tell you a bit more about myself and why I’m running. [But if that’s all you needed to hear and you’re ready to get to work, please chip in whatever you can – split between my campaign and Chris Deluzio – to help hit our $1 million launch goal and become a Founding Donor of my campaign to keep Michigan blue.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106293109/541045058/-1222209541?refcode=email_042225_deluziostevens&amounts=5,25,50,100,250,500,1000&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjU0MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmZDQ4NzZhMy04ZTFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Sjaaz-kp3OirTfFIQwIbfcnzmQddgK81LBhfMjPNobQ=)** | | [CHIP IN →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106293111/541045061/-1222209541?refcode=email_042225_deluziostevens&amounts=5,25,50,100,250,500,1000&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjU0MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmZDQ4NzZhMy04ZTFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Sjaaz-kp3OirTfFIQwIbfcnzmQddgK81LBhfMjPNobQ=)

I’m proud to be a lifelong Michigander. I learned the value of hard work by watching my parents – who owned their own landscaping business – build things. Heavy machinery equipment, bobcats, plows, dirt, grease, and grime – it was all part of my childhood.
Later in life, I got the call to give back to the state I love during a time of great uncertainty: the Great Recession.**I can’t tell you how unfathomable it was to hear the words “bankruptcy” and “General Motors” in the same sentence.** So I stepped up to do my part and served as chief of staff for the Auto Rescue initiative under President Obama.

We brought workers, corporations, and union leadership around the same table to stabilize the auto industry. On Friday nights, I’d stay in the office until the late evening and return every call from every Michigander who called our office worried about the future. _In the end, we saved 200,000 Michigan jobs._

I can’t help but see parallels between then and now as we find ourselves in another moment of great uncertainty, thanks to the chaos forced on us by Donald Trump and his billionaire buddy Elon Musk.

People are rightly concerned about rising costs, shoot-from-the-hip tariffs, and attacks on our personal freedoms. **Michiganders need a fighter in their corner – and that’s who I’ve been my entire life.**

| ''The five-person Democrat majority on the Pennridge School Board is poised to make a significant policy change this month, which would allow school instructional time to be used to administer third-party surveys from outside organizations.

>From Planned Parenthood to CHOP’s Gender and Sexuality Development Clinic, as long as the administration deems a survey supportive of “social and emotional development,” the changes to Policy 235.1 would permit such surveys to be administered to Pennridge students of all ages. This policy change is so extreme that it is not even recommended by the Pennsylvania School Board Association..."

Happy Earth Day, Peter — it’s Valerie Foushee

This Earth Day, I’m thinking about our commitment to protecting our planet so that our future generations can live with clean air, water, and safety from climate disasters.

From the gorgeous trees and waterfalls of the Great Smokey Mountains to the sandy beaches and islands of the Outer Banks, these natural landscapes bring beauty and jobs to the Tar Heel State — and we MUST protect them from climate change.

But we’re all seeing what’s happening.

Extreme weather patterns are causing hurricanes and flooding that are destroying North Carolina’s homes and national parks. Rising sea levels and erosion are threatening public infrastructure and changing our coastlines and natural ecosystems.

That’s why in Congress, I’m doing everything I can to address climate change. [Will you sign my personal petition if you’re with me in this fight?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106295967/541052907/-3983535?source=SBD_VF_EM_PET_042225_EarthDay_180DO_D1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTc5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjNmE3ZGNmYS05MjFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=rDdYedza6wPmimsp-eo5CtPNzy5cjYtQVT0C5xtu1_g=&emci=89ddbbf4-921f-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&emdi=c6a7dcfa-921f-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&ceid=799895) | [SIGN ON](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106295969/541052909/-3983535?source=SBD_VF_EM_PET_042225_EarthDay_180DO_D1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTc5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjNmE3ZGNmYS05MjFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=rDdYedza6wPmimsp-eo5CtPNzy5cjYtQVT0C5xtu1_g=&emci=89ddbbf4-921f-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&emdi=c6a7dcfa-921f-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&ceid=799895)

As a member of the Sustainable Energy & Environment Coalition, I’m fighting to strengthen environmental protection laws and protect agencies like FEMA that help North Carolina prepare and recover from climate disasters.

As a member of the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, I’m working to build sustainable energy infrastructure and invest in green transportation.

But with Trump going all out to undermine environmental protections and slash funding for climate disaster relief, we need to go ALL OUT to stop this disaster of an administration. [So in the spirit of Earth Day, will you sign my petition to demand Congress to address climate change and protect our communities from disasters like hurricanes? ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106295971/541052970/-3983535?source=SBD_VF_EM_PET_042225_EarthDay_180DO_D1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTc5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjNmE3ZGNmYS05MjFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=rDdYedza6wPmimsp-eo5CtPNzy5cjYtQVT0C5xtu1_g=&emci=89ddbbf4-921f-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&emdi=c6a7dcfa-921f-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&ceid=799895)

At COURIER, we’re already doing the work — calling Trump’s actions what they are, highlighting the power of protest, and refusing to provide cover for authoritarianism.

The Trump regime is defying the courts. Federal agents are grabbing people off the streets and jailing them for exercising their 1st Amendment rights. Trump is extorting universities and law firms.
It’s a dictatorship-in-progress.
The mainstream news media have helped bring us to this disaster with both-sidesing, sane-washing, and cheap fascination with Trump’s supposed “entertainment” skills. They had a duty to warn, and they largely failed. If our democracy goes down, legacy news outlets will be a key reason why.
But it’s not too late. We’ve seen pushback from some Democratic leaders (though not enough), rulings by principled judges, and a people-power movement gathering steam. Legitimate news outlets should be a part of the defense of democracy, too. Journalists know how to do this. It’s a question of whether their corporate bosses will let them. Here’s what I urge the media to do:
**1\. Say directly that Trump is overthrowing democracy. Lose the weasel-wording.**

The drip-drip-drip of news stories can be exhausting, and some people tune out. The media must get them to understand that all the individual outrages add up to one huge threat to the future of our families and our country. Most people aren’t getting that message when the New York Times’ euphemism desk describes Trump’s authoritarianism as “a maximalist view of his powers,” or when the Washington Post refers to “Trump’s ever-shifting relationship with the Constitution.”
What’s happening now is one of the worst crises in American history. So act like it, media. Write sweeping stories with straightforward headlines that use words like “dictatorship,” “authoritarian,” and “lawless.”
A New York Times headline over the weekend saying that Trump was “Defying the Law and the Courts” gave us some hope that major media might finally be waking up. That story was the first time the Times had used the term “convicted felon” to describe Trump in nearly three months.
****[Donate now](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106296154/541053450/-1581427288?refcode=20250421_MarkJacobs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNmRkZTNmZDQtOTIxZi1mMDExLThiM2QtMDAyMjQ4MmE5ZmI3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=fBXfcaLnCsKolNYBdr480kSngN6xShY2PHYdP5-4j94=)****
**2\. Cover the mass protests as major news.**
It’s frustrating when journalists are bored by seeing people get off their couches and into the streets to express their love for their country. Shallow journalists would rather write about tweets than about a crowd of protesters stretching many blocks down New York’s Fifth Avenue.
An example of media myopia came after the April 5 Hands off rallies when National Public Radio’s public editor, Kelly McBride, defended NPR’s coverage by saying the protests by 3 million people were no big deal. “I went to watch the demonstration in Manhattan so I could judge the newsworthiness myself,” she wrote. “As a news event, it wasn’t very compelling.”
Her logic was mind-blowingly flawed. “Statistically,” she wrote, “most news consumers are not protesting: Of the 300+ million people in the U.S., approximately 3 million protested last Saturday at 1,400 locations.” By that logic, the media shouldn’t cover the NBA playoffs because hardly any news consumers are playing in it.
Protests this past weekend were probably smaller in total numbers, but they were still very well attended at hundreds of locations. Coverage was mixed: hard to find on the New York Times website, but fairly prominent in the Washington Post, NPR, and other outlets.
This outpouring of patriotism is an antidote to widespread disaffection with politics. It’s exciting – and newsworthy.

******3\. Treat White House briefings as the travesty they are.******

Trump and his lying press secretary, Karoline Leavitt, are harassing the Associated Press and other mainstream outlets, using access as a weapon. And they’re getting away with it because the White House Correspondents’ Association hasn’t found an effective response. Meanwhile, Trump is bringing in ringers – right-wing pseudo-journalists who say things to Leavitt like “You look great. You’re doing a great job.”
Yet mainstream reporters keep joining the circus. When they play their part and fail to push back aggressively on Trump’s blatant lies, they’re doing worse than nothing. Their presence at his briefings provides an air of legitimacy, of normalcy.
News outlets should do one of these three things:
1. Boycott the briefings.
2. Send interns to the briefings to roll tape but not ask questions.
3. Send top reporters to the briefings and have them aggressively dispute Team Trump’s lies, including interrupting the liars in the middle of sentences. If the reporters get kicked out, they get kicked out. But they’ll be fighting for the truth, not serving as scenery for Trump’s dishonesty.

Whatever the journalists do, it can’t go on like this.
**[Support Independent Journalism](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106296155/541053451/-1581427288?refcode=20250421_MarkJacobs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNmRkZTNmZDQtOTIxZi1mMDExLThiM2QtMDAyMjQ4MmE5ZmI3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=fBXfcaLnCsKolNYBdr480kSngN6xShY2PHYdP5-4j94=)**
****4\. Show how Trump’s cuts will hurt people.****
****** **
The news of Trump’s political vandalism isn’t just a Washington story, and it doesn’t affect only federal workers. Interview someone whose life was saved because of an early warning about a tornado – the type of warning that may come later or not at all because of National Weather Service cuts. Talk to a victim of a credit card scam who got a refund because of action by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, which Trump is eviscerating. Highlight a child who is thriving in school because of the Head Start program, which Trump has targeted for extinction.
Put a human face on the story.
******5\. Emphasize that fascism is bad for the economy.******
****** **
This is not hard to do, considering how Trump’s tariffs are battering the previously healthy financial picture. It’s not just that Trump’s policies are incompetent – it’s that his regime is riddled with corruption, which is toxic to the free enterprise system. People may not fully realize the threat of a dictatorship, but they know when their grocery prices go up. It’s up to the media to tell them why prices are going up.

The point of journalism is to deliver facts that improve people’s lives. Tolerance for dishonesty, corruption, and authoritarianism does just the opposite. When the nation’s founders put press freedom in the Constitution, they created both a right and an obligation for journalists. It’s getting late for corporate media to do their duty.**[Contribute now to support journalism like this](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106296156/541053452/-1581427288?refcode=20250421_MarkJacobs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNmRkZTNmZDQtOTIxZi1mMDExLThiM2QtMDAyMjQ4MmE5ZmI3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=fBXfcaLnCsKolNYBdr480kSngN6xShY2PHYdP5-4j94=)**
