clean_body: The Trump regime is defying the courts. Federal agents are grabbing people off the streets and jailing them for exercising their 1st Amendment rights. Trump is extorting universities and law firms. Hi — Mark Jacob here, contributor at COURIER. It’s not too late for the mainstream media to seek redemption — but time is running out. As Trump defies the courts, jails protesters, and extorts universities, the media must stop acting like this is normal. In today’s piece, I laid out five ways major outlets can start doing their duty before it’s too late. At COURIER, we’re already doing the work — calling Trump’s actions what they are, highlighting the power of protest, and refusing to provide cover for authoritarianism. = = Thanks for being in this fight, Mark Jacob COURIER Contributor The Trump regime is defying the courts. Federal agents are grabbing people off the streets and jailing them for exercising their 1st Amendment rights. Trump is extorting universities and law firms. It’s a dictatorship-in-progress. The mainstream news media have helped bring us to this disaster with both-sidesing, sane-washing, and cheap fascination with Trump’s supposed “entertainment” skills. They had a duty to warn, and they largely failed. If our democracy goes down, legacy news outlets will be a key reason why. But it’s not too late. We’ve seen pushback from some Democratic leaders (though not enough), rulings by principled judges, and a people-power movement gathering steam. Legitimate news outlets should be a part of the defense of democracy, too. Journalists know how to do this. It’s a question of whether their corporate bosses will let them. Here’s what I urge the media to do: 1\. Say directly that Trump is overthrowing democracy. Lose the weasel-wording. The drip-drip-drip of news stories can be exhausting, and some people tune out. The media must get them to understand that all the individual outrages add up to one huge threat to the future of our families and our country. Most people aren’t getting that message when the New York Times’ euphemism desk describes Trump’s authoritarianism as “a maximalist view of his powers,” or when the Washington Post refers to “Trump’s ever-shifting relationship with the Constitution.” What’s happening now is one of the worst crises in American history. So act like it, media. Write sweeping stories with straightforward headlines that use words like “dictatorship,” “authoritarian,” and “lawless.” A New York Times headline over the weekend saying that Trump was “Defying the Law and the Courts” gave us some hope that major media might finally be waking up. That story was the first time the Times had used the term “convicted felon” to describe Trump in nearly three months. = 2\. Cover the mass protests as major news. It’s frustrating when journalists are bored by seeing people get off their couches and into the streets to express their love for their country. Shallow journalists would rather write about tweets than about a crowd of protesters stretching many blocks down New York’s Fifth Avenue. An example of media myopia came after the April 5 Hands off rallies when National Public Radio’s public editor, Kelly McBride, defended NPR’s coverage by saying the protests by 3 million people were no big deal. “I went to watch the demonstration in Manhattan so I could judge the newsworthiness myself,” she wrote. “As a news event, it wasn’t very compelling.” Her logic was mind-blowingly flawed. “Statistically,” she wrote, “most news consumers are not protesting: Of the 300+ million people in the U.S., approximately 3 million protested last Saturday at 1,400 locations.” By that logic, the media shouldn’t cover the NBA playoffs because hardly any news consumers are playing in it. Protests this past weekend were probably smaller in total numbers, but they were still very well attended at hundreds of locations. Coverage was mixed: hard to find on the New York Times website, but fairly prominent in the Washington Post, NPR, and other outlets. This outpouring of patriotism is an antidote to widespread disaffection with politics. It’s exciting – and newsworthy. **3\. Treat White House briefings as the travesty they are.** Trump and his lying press secretary, Karoline Leavitt, are harassing the Associated Press and other mainstream outlets, using access as a weapon. And they’re getting away with it because the White House Correspondents’ Association hasn’t found an effective response. Meanwhile, Trump is bringing in ringers – right-wing pseudo-journalists who say things to Leavitt like “You look great. You’re doing a great job.” Yet mainstream reporters keep joining the circus. When they play their part and fail to push back aggressively on Trump’s blatant lies, they’re doing worse than nothing. Their presence at his briefings provides an air of legitimacy, of normalcy. News outlets should do one of these three things: 1. Boycott the briefings. 2. Send interns to the briefings to roll tape but not ask questions. 3. Send top reporters to the briefings and have them aggressively dispute Team Trump’s lies, including interrupting the liars in the middle of sentences. If the reporters get kicked out, they get kicked out. But they’ll be fighting for the truth, not serving as scenery for Trump’s dishonesty. Whatever the journalists do, it can’t go on like this. = 4\. Show how Trump’s cuts will hurt people. ** The news of Trump’s political vandalism isn’t just a Washington story, and it doesn’t affect only federal workers. Interview someone whose life was saved because of an early warning about a tornado – the type of warning that may come later or not at all because of National Weather Service cuts. Talk to a victim of a credit card scam who got a refund because of action by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, which Trump is eviscerating. Highlight a child who is thriving in school because of the Head Start program, which Trump has targeted for extinction. Put a human face on the story. ****5\. Emphasize that fascism is bad for the economy.** ** This is not hard to do, considering how Trump’s tariffs are battering the previously healthy financial picture. It’s not just that Trump’s policies are incompetent – it’s that his regime is riddled with corruption, which is toxic to the free enterprise system. People may not fully realize the threat of a dictatorship, but they know when their grocery prices go up. It’s up to the media to tell them why prices are going up. The point of journalism is to deliver facts that improve people’s lives. Tolerance for dishonesty, corruption, and authoritarianism does just the opposite. When the nation’s founders put press freedom in the Constitution, they created both a right and an obligation for journalists. It’s getting late for corporate media to do their duty.= Email us: mailto:info@couriernewsroom.com

Friend, It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 __and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. **Now, I'm grateful to again serve as an Honorary Grand Marshal on the 20th anniversary of this important event.** This year will be a remembrance like no other, as we commemorate the 80th anniversary of victory in World War II and the 250th birthdays of the U.S. Army, Navy, and Marine Corps. **[Friend, the National Memorial Day Parade is ENTIRELY FUNDED by private contributions, including from generous Americans like you. Will you help chip in today to help support the Parade with a gift of $25, $50, $75, $150, or more?](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=c56dcb1d757147d3930c6b7d85b2c7d0&_e=WXK-USaT8F0hplmmlVvH-FQGCzI0b38zYgujEXHABEqejND-wnxQEtKf1bSWMpq33nwFv-A5CNRxmGvPKAUqoH5ZP7WRKo6whEodbFbeu-uTrDyux3hOk-9oNDfnbnr02LIhShbyDNKrL5R5Yky7SQZOSzYRjFiVQatZ-pvarQOHXC33DnSqPk9DUbBlVvGi3qhCbY48mnB7tCU3pWurL3NGvj4aqMWDIisvaCDMBRKQGz2tsUcNwdvhdLSYZgOsZQbn2QjCxLbRwKQMcy4TWZ7c-zjCTFZM20JRtK3MGYF7tdtgOvMWGNed9cE8cs23)**

[](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=c56dcb1d757147d3930c6b7d85b2c7d0&_e=WXK-USaT8F0hplmmlVvH-FQGCzI0b38zYgujEXHABEqejND-wnxQEtKf1bSWMpq33nwFv-A5CNRxmGvPKAUqoH5ZP7WRKo6whEodbFbeu-uTrDyux3hOk-9oNDfnbnr02LIhShbyDNKrL5R5Yky7SQZOSzYRjFiVQatZ-pvarQNp5OVCGCFiSp34xIa-hgtV0ORZEIPUOXyMciRyoLbpX_2qhu1AClkqn3XMm8-PXZpfvjDCJSt9Jov2Pi82v5LthFf4j_Hj7IgVJonUS1I5jORs7E8SVR4EOXU4Mc5gDSnvFdYzpDrUn5aGGKbMEp2o)
---
The National Memorial Day Parade costs a fraction of other major public events to put on each year. In fact, _the entire parade_ costs about as much as just THREE balloons in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade or TWO floats in the Rose Bowl Parade! _That means that every dollar that 's contributed by a generous American like you makes a difference for this important event._ **But I want to reiterate that American Veterans Center does not take ANY federal funding for this event. It is funded _entirely_ by private citizens like you who want to honor those who have sacrificed so much for our country.** Your support of the American Veterans Center not only helps the Parade, but also supports great programs like:
* Record hundreds of oral histories of veterans from World War II to Today before we lose these stories forever.

* Hold our National Youth Summit which allows young students a chance to hear first-hand from veterans from WWII, Korea, and Vietnam.

* Produce veteran focused T.V. documentaries and specials that remind Americans the price of our freedom.

[](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=c56dcb1d757147d3930c6b7d85b2c7d0&_e=WXK-USaT8F0hplmmlVvH-FQGCzI0b38zYgujEXHABEqejND-wnxQEtKf1bSWMpq3XBZm-goZU0ONc5OiNSMRIqj-ntujQQFm5RMqMce3cjHWyv9BIusBw9bwsI6693VzDy_7_z4Sp1kTeRR-P73DP6nTzyPW4XIe3O110ny8C77Y0j0O_V9sN6jrHOSsbGHGbgXALKV5ovp7JnuG2feHOP3t0TssYzYUjpVcm-w6UJUtm0vg1pfOYGhYb7Wk3WeYvC1M8tcpAgZAOyXjK-DuQiD-bzNCtlYwK7s36plvpvk%3D)[**Please join me in support of the National Memorial Day Parade with a gift of $25, $50, $75, $150, $250, $500, or more right now.**](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=c56dcb1d757147d3930c6b7d85b2c7d0&_e=WXK-USaT8F0hplmmlVvH-FQGCzI0b38zYgujEXHABEqejND-wnxQEtKf1bSWMpq33nwFv-A5CNRxmGvPKAUqoH5ZP7WRKo6whEodbFbeu-uTrDyux3hOk-9oNDfnbnr02LIhShbyDNKrL5R5Yky7SQZOSzYRjFiVQatZ-pvarQNHS_Ei8dd1Oot0UA4MuT_1xDRRlo0Ri3pobMIosaeSiUj3psXK3KNQEj35GmlIh9YmTgwp8SAlosQWA9hdfq_dD3HVzDADnESgdR8DSdV17TVxRCGswVdxJlnKVAmYLYQ27yZWk5ad-9gGoANajaaS) If you've been looking for an opportunity to give back to those who have given so much for our freedom, this is one of the best possible ways you could do it. _And for a special group of veterans, this might be one of the last chances we get._ You see, with each year that goes by, we lose more and more of our World War II veterans, and for the few we have remaining, traveling to Washington, D.C., for the parade is difficult. WWII veterans were a key part of the first parade when it was revived in 2005, as they have been every year since for the last 20 years. _But this may be the last year we have the opportunity to have these brave men and women with us for the parade._** ** **That's why we are making a concerted effort to ensure these veterans are at this year's National Memorial Day Parade to honor them one last time. ** So this year, as we mark the 80th anniversary of victory in Europe and Japan to end World War II - and the 250th anniversaries of the Army, Navy, and Marine Corps - I encourage you to help us honor these brave veterans while we still have them with us.
---
[ **Support the National Memorial Day Parade**](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=c56dcb1d757147d3930c6b7d85b2c7d0&_e=WXK-USaT8F0hplmmlVvH-FQGCzI0b38zYgujEXHABEqejND-wnxQEtKf1bSWMpq33nwFv-A5CNRxmGvPKAUqoH5ZP7WRKo6whEodbFbeu-uTrDyux3hOk-9oNDfnbnr02LIhShbyDNKrL5R5Yky7SQZOSzYRjFiVQatZ-pvarQMihvWyDE27CmQPYVNsqHyhxiq8NF_aA60OCqcvLX-Xhda2yOG5CBAAi_tDhPIXjTe5xINBawpCMOzty8danZ8kMM7H7x8GWRdymZGUSijfj2PbnnHsi0Y17sVhKQ6cQXx-yFqjmjiaWARKj585hAmz)
---
And no matter how much you can give to this important cause, I want to ask something additional of you. On Memorial Day - not just this momentous year of military milestones, but every year - please join me in honoring those who made the ultimate sacrifice for our freedoms. Come to the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. Visit a local veterans' cemetery. Send a note to a family of the fallen. Or simply take a quiet moment to think about the men and women who gave their lives to defend OUR country. _I believe that while we can never do enough to express our gratitude to our defenders, veterans, and first responders, we can always do a little more._ _**[Friend, thank you for your support of America's heroes, and please - if you're able, make a gift to fund the National Memorial Day Parade right now during its 20th anniversary.](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=c56dcb1d757147d3930c6b7d85b2c7d0&_e=WXK-USaT8F0hplmmlVvH-FQGCzI0b38zYgujEXHABEqejND-wnxQEtKf1bSWMpq33nwFv-A5CNRxmGvPKAUqoH5ZP7WRKo6whEodbFbeu-uTrDyux3hOk-9oNDfnbnr02LIhShbyDNKrL5R5Yky7SQZOSzYRjFiVQatZ-pvarQNMBw3MdcdAGdaG4sYB8yw98AvmcLwidJjlu6hVgzhpUmacI1Kk8_Ea7Z-OXtG8_r3PNUNchFo3cNvqNOlPLMydqu2ukUwpSak0srA0ptF_uwVePZeEBUK1muy_ZRTTG-6Reda6_jEbA81bBMzANeF8)**_ Sincerely, Gary SiniseHonorary Grand MarshalNational Memorial Day Parade

But fossil fuels aren't the only force harming the planet. We also need to take on plastic pollution with a bold, binding global plastics treaty. We are drowning in plastics that are littering our beaches, destroying our ecosystems, and poisoning human health. **We need action, and we need it now. clean_body: We need action, and we need it now. | | | | On this Earth Day, we can't just celebrate — we also need to be sounding the alarm. While we made historic investments in protecting the planet and reducing greenhouse gas emissions under President Biden, that progress is at risk. The fight for a livable future is far from over. We still have a LOT of work to do to continue to take on the climate crisis — and Trump and his Cabinet of fossil-fuel cronies are hellbent on taking us backward as fast as they can. We need to end the world's addiction to fossil fuels. We are flooding the world with dangerous, planet-warming carbon dioxide and other gases from burning fossil fuels. Trump is making this problem worse day by day. But fossil fuels aren't the only force harming the planet. We also need to take on plastic pollution with a bold, binding global plastics treaty. We are drowning in plastics that are littering our beaches, destroying our ecosystems, and poisoning human health. We need action, and we need it now. And that's why I will always use every tool I have — from legislation to oversight to appropriations to speaking out — to ensure a sustainable future for generations to come. So, on Earth Day, let's rededicate ourselves to a rapid and just transition to renewable energy and an end to the production of fossil fuels, to action on plastic pollution, and to educating America about the need to preserve our planet's precious biodiversity. This Earth Day, here's how you can help: make choices that reflect the future you believe in. Plant a tree, pick up litter, and make a plan to use less plastic. But don't stop there. Join with others, organize, and push for bold change. A livable planet is within reach if we fight for it together. Onward! A healthy environment is vital to Washingtonians’ way of life and the regional economy, so mitigating climate change must be a top priority.

| | It is Earth Day. Our district is one of the most scenic and diverse in the country. From rolling hills, stunning valleys, and beautiful landscapes along the Puget Sound and the Salish Sea to our diverse ecosystem that supports large migrations of shore birds, beloved salmon returns, and the iconic bald eagle. Northwest Washington is beloved by environmentalists and adventurers alike. **Beyond the stunning scenery, our landscapes and natural resources are a key component of our local economy.** The rivers throughout the district have deposited rich soils that contribute to some of the finest agricultural land in the country. Northwest Washington's fertile soil must be cared for and protected. Further, our district's proximity to the Pacific Ocean makes our coastal communities major economic centers, and we have a responsibility to protect ocean habitats and scenic shorelines through thoughtful policy-making and clean energy innovation. **Right now, some of our greatest progress on climate change, environmental justice, energy policy, public health, public land, and wildlife conservation is under attack.** Their efforts to undermine our progress make days like today even more important to acknowledge. I firmly believe that these issues must be a top priority. Here is some of the progress we have made in Congress in the past few years:
* I helped draft and pass the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, which allocates $5.3 billion over five years to provide Washingtonians with more transportation options, ease congestion in local communities, and reduce carbon pollution across the state, in addition to allocating nearly $370 million this year to invest in the state's transit agencies and communities.
* I introduced and helped pass the Migratory Birds of the Americas Conservation Enhancements Act, a bipartisan bill to help protect diverse bird populations and their habitats in the Pacific Northwest and across the Western Hemisphere.
* I supported the bipartisan Water Resources Development Act of 2022 because protecting our natural environment is especially critical to maintaining a healthy economy and community.

**As we deal with warmer temperatures, rising sea levels, and climate-caused disasters, I will continue working to ensure our infrastructure can handle the changing climate and keep our communities safe.** Happy Earth Day. clean_body: A healthy environment is vital to Washingtonians’ way of life and the regional economy, so mitigating climate change must be a top priority. | | | | It is Earth Day. Our district is one of the most scenic and diverse in the country. From rolling hills, stunning valleys, and beautiful landscapes along the Puget Sound and the Salish Sea to our diverse ecosystem that supports large migrations of shore birds, beloved salmon returns, and the iconic bald eagle. Northwest Washington is beloved by environmentalists and adventurers alike. Beyond the stunning scenery, our landscapes and natural resources are a key component of our local economy. The rivers throughout the district have deposited rich soils that contribute to some of the finest agricultural land in the country. Northwest Washington's fertile soil must be cared for and protected. Further, our district's proximity to the Pacific Ocean makes our coastal communities major economic centers, and we have a responsibility to protect ocean habitats and scenic shorelines through thoughtful policy-making and clean energy innovation. Right now, some of our greatest progress on climate change, environmental justice, energy policy, public health, public land, and wildlife conservation is under attack. Their efforts to undermine our progress make days like today even more important to acknowledge. I firmly believe that these issues must be a top priority. Here is some of the progress we have made in Congress in the past few years: I helped draft and pass the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, which allocates $5.3 billion over five years to provide Washingtonians with more transportation options, ease congestion in local communities, and reduce carbon pollution across the state, in addition to allocating nearly $370 million this year to invest in the state's transit agencies and communities. I introduced and helped pass the Migratory Birds of the Americas Conservation Enhancements Act, a bipartisan bill to help protect diverse bird populations and their habitats in the Pacific Northwest and across the Western Hemisphere. I supported the bipartisan Water Resources Development Act of 2022 because protecting our natural environment is especially critical to maintaining a healthy economy and community. As we deal with warmer temperatures, rising sea levels, and climate-caused disasters, I will continue working to ensure our infrastructure can handle the changing climate and keep our communities safe. Happy Earth Day. ## Straightening out the spin room...
There's been lot of talk in the media recently about a Maryland father who was "accidentally deported" and is now in an El Salvador prison.
Sounds pretty awful, right?
It would be, if that was an honest characterization. But what is the truth?
The man in question, Kilmar Abrego Garcia, has many defining characteristics. He's a citizen of El Salvador, a member of the notorious MS-13 gang, an illegal alien, and an alleged repeat violent wife-beater.
All that aside, based on his record of repeated domestic abuse, Abrego Garcia was marked eligible for deportation as early as 2019 - and he had a lawful deportation order at the time of his deportation.
Yet the term the media chose to describe him was "Maryland man," "Maryland father."
Conservatives are fighting back against the shameless spin, just take this *edited* NYT article that the White House X account shared last week:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/923760d1-bd78-4225-9ad8-1d16baa076a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Winning in Michigan is essential to regaining our Democratic Senate majority, and right now The Cook Political Report is rating our race as a “Toss Up.” That means we’re _already_ one of the GOP’s top targets for defeat. generations. Public lands belong to the people, not corporate polluters — and they are NOT

body:

| |
---
|
---
| Dear Friend, Over the past two weeks, the Mississippi Center for Public Policy has spotlighted lawmakers who stood boldly for freedom during the 2025 legislative session. Today we honor two exceptional leaders whose impact cannot be overstated.

**Senator Angela Hill – Senate Hero**
---
|
---
_Senator Angela Hill presented with the Mississippi Freedom Award_
| Sen. Hill has long been a fierce defender of liberty. This session, she led the charge against divisive DEI initiatives and stood firm for education reform and individual rights. Her courage, consistency, and commitment to principle make her a standout leader in the fight for Mississippi’s future. We are proud to name her our 2025 Senate Hero.

**Representative Jason White – House Hero**
---
|
---
_Speaker of the House Jason White presented with the Mississippi Freedom Award_
| As Speaker of the House, Rep. White is pursuing a pro growth agenda. He was a driving force behind income tax elimination. His vision for a more prosperous Mississippi and his ability to unify and advance key reforms make him a winner.

It is only fitting we conclude this year’s Awards with two individuals who not only supported change but drove it forward.

Though this concludes our official recognitions for the session, the work of building a freer Mississippi continues—and we’re just getting started.

The forces for reform are winning. The forces of the status quo are in retreat.
Thank you for standing with us in this mission.
---

As the only directly elected regional government in the United States, Metro has helped shape the political, economic, social, and built landscape of the Portland metropolitan area since 1979. Working with communities, businesses, and leaders across 24 cities and 3 counties, Metro addresses issues related to land use, transportation, garbage and recycling, parks and nature, economic development, and cultural amenities. **Metro is core to building and protecting democracy, starting from a local level.** _The zoo, managed by Metro, now welcomes more than 1.6 million visitors each year_ Because it can bridge jurisdictional boundaries, Metro is in a unique position to move the region forward. For example, we're authorized by Congress and the State of Oregon to coordinate and plan investments in the transportation system across the three counties. That has allowed the region to expand transportation options, make our streets safer for everyone, and improve existing public transit service. _Earlier this year, Metro and partners were awarded $4 million to advance community-centered investments on 82nd Avenue and Tualatin Valley Highway_ **Metro's collaboration with cities, counties, and transportation agencies to invest federal highway and public transit funds is just one of the community-based ways we lead the region forward.** [**You can help shape our community's future by learning about local Metro projects in your Hi, Peter – this is Congresswoman Haley Stevens writing to you with exciting news: Today, I’m launching my campaign for Michigan’s open U.S. Senate seat.

Winning in Michigan is essential to regaining our Democratic Senate majority, and right now The Cook Political Report is rating our race as a “Toss Up.” That means we’re already one of the GOP’s top targets for defeat. Just last year, they spent nearly $80 million trying to buy Michigan’s Senate seat and came up only 0.3% short, so I need your early support to win.

**Peter, I want to tell you a bit more about myself and why I’m running.** [_**But if that’s all you needed to hear and you’re ready to get to work, please chip in whatever you can – split between my campaign and Rep. I’m proud to be a lifelong Michigander. I learned the value of hard work by watching my parents – who owned their own landscaping business – build things. Heavy machinery equipment, bobcats, plows, dirt, grease, and grime – it was all part of my childhood.

Later in life, I got the call to give back to the state I love during a time of great uncertainty: the Great Recession. **I can’t tell you how unfathomable it was to hear the words “bankruptcy” and “General Motors” in the same sentence.** So I stepped up to do my part and served as chief of staff for the Auto Rescue initiative under President Obama.

We brought workers, corporations, and union leadership around the same table to stabilize the auto industry. On Friday nights, I’d stay in the office until the late evening and return every call from every Michigander who called our office worried about the future. In the end, we saved 200,000 Michigan jobs.

I can’t help but see parallels between then and now as we find ourselves in another moment of great uncertainty, thanks to the chaos forced on us by Donald Trump and his billionaire buddy Elon Musk.

People are rightly concerned about rising costs, shoot-from-the-hip tariffs, and attacks on our personal freedoms. **Michiganders need a fighter in their corner – and that’s who I’ve been my entire life.**

[_**If you’re ready to fight with me – to win this battleground race, take back the Senate majority, and stop Trump – can you split a grassroots donation between my campaign and Rep. Laura Gillen? I learned the value of hard work by watching my parents – who owned their own landscaping business – build things. Heavy machinery equipment, bobcats, plows, dirt, grease, and grime – it was all part of my childhood. Later in life, I got the call to give back to the state I love during a time of great uncertainty: the Great Recession. I can’t tell you how unfathomable it was to hear the words “bankruptcy” and “General Motors” in the same sentence. In the end, we saved 200,000 Michigan jobs. name: David Hogg
subject: Enraging
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
We can’t allow ourselves to be desensitized to this.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20250422-1&t=1&akid=2025%2E587540%2EJ5NkX3)
Peter, we cannot allow ourselves to be desensitized to headlines like this one:
**This should not be our normal.** We should not fear for our lives every time that we go to school in this country. But the United States is one of the only places in the world where this phenomenon keeps happening. And our leaders are failing us.
Just three weeks ago, Florida Republicans voted to repeal gun safety measures that we won after the tragedy at Parkland – _even as school shootings continue._
In the Oval Office, reporters asked President Trump about what was at the time an active shooting. He called the shooting “a shame” and “a horrible thing” before adding: _“Things like this take place.”_ In other words, **don’t expect any action.** It’s disgusting that we have moved on from “thoughts and prayers” to “I don’t care.”
It’s enraging that this keeps happening, in Florida and everywhere else. _We can’t accept it_ – we have to keep fighting for the life-saving policy changes needed in Florida and across the country before more people are senselessly slaughtered.
As someone who experienced a shooting at my high school, I want to help create a world where no one has to live through what my community had to back in 2018. And clearly, that means replacing the **_do-nothing dinosaurs_** running this country.
Together, we can elect the next generation of leaders who won’t cower before the gun lobby, but will fight for meaningful gun reform legislation to keep us all safe.
I want to personally thank everyone who is standing with us in this fight. Lives are literally hanging in the balance – that’s how important our work really is, Peter.
Thank you,
David Hogg

| | It is my firm opinion that schools have NO jurisdiction or business teaching material regarding SEXUAL BEHAVIOR or MENTAL HEALTH. Schools have ZERO authority to reframe the narrative in our children's minds for what is considered "normal, moral, or acceptable" sexual behavior or expression. These topics are highly personal, individual, and should be addressed by parents according their own beliefs. They also should not be collecting private health data and information on your children via surveys and questionnaires.
---
| | The School Board cited "attendance issues" as a reason for their refusal of parental rights.Which leads me to another question...Just how often is this sort of material being presented to our children who are supposed to be learning the basics of reading, writing, arithmetic?

| | No wonder our kids are more confused, more depressed, more anxious and more medicated than ever. The next generation is being shaped as we speak. As parents, the future of our Commonwealth and nation rests on our shoulders. We must defend their minds and bodies from destructive ideologies that lead to self harm, spiritual brokeness, and mental health crises.
---
| | If elected as Delegate, protecting our children is a hill I'm willing to die on. I will relentlessly defend your parental authority, and pledge to never take a vote that goes against your God-given religious or parental rights as recognized in the Constitution and Virginia Code (see below).

#

Hi, Peter – if you haven’t gotten to know me yet, my name is Haley Stevens, and I’m running for Michigan’s U.S. Senate seat to fight for the people I love in the state that I love.
I’ve had the honor of representing Michigan’s 11th Congressional District in the House since 2019. It means everything to me to serve my state in Congress. But as I’ve traveled around our great state, it’s clear that the people I love are afraid. _They’re afraid because of the chaos and uncertainty that Donald Trump and Elon Musk have inflicted upon our nation._
All across our state I hear concerns about rising costs, fear of the uncertainty in our auto industry caused by reckless shoot-from-the-hip tariffs, and worries about the future of Social Security and Medicare. And you better believe people are outright disturbed by Trump’s attacks on our democracy and personal freedoms.

name: Deb Haaland
subject: All of our progress is at risk.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO
body:
I will be a fierce defender of our home, but I can’t win without your support.
# [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/133?t=1&akid=1489%2E400544%2EvLbPgT)
**Today is Earth Day** – a time to celebrate our planet and recommit to protecting the lands, waters, and natural resources that sustain us.
_**For me, this fight is personal.**_
My ancestors came to the high desert of New Mexico and kick-started a thriving agricultural tradition. I grew up fishing with my dad and running through the mesas with my cousins. It was there I learned what it means to be a steward of the Earth and to care for our land, wildlife, and natural resources – not just for ourselves, but for the generations to come.
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_dh_20250422_1_earthday?refcode=em20250422-1489&:amount=5&refcode2=1489_400544_vLbPgT&akid=1489%2E400544%2EvLbPgT)
As Secretary of the Interior, I carried that lesson with me every day. And I’m proud that over four years, we helped protect more lands and waters than any administration in U.S. history while also creating good jobs in clean energy, conservation, and cleaning up legacy pollution.
But now, _all of that progress is at risk._
Donald Trump and Elon Musk are scheming to auction our public lands to the highest bidder. They have worked to gut environmental protections and sell off sacred lands. They even tried to fire our dedicated National Parks and National Forests workers.
Governors are a critical line of defense against the Trump agenda, especially when it comes to standing up against the attacks on our environment. **And as governor, I will be a fierce defender of our home, but I can’t win without your support.**
**[That’s why, this Earth Day, I’m asking you to chip in $5 to help power our grassroots campaign and protect New Mexico’s land, water, and future.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_dh_20250422_1_earthday?amount=5&refcode=em20250422-1489&refcode2=1489_400544_vLbPgT&akid=1489%2E400544%2EvLbPgT)**

In solidarity,
Deb

clean_body: President Trump is back in office. Let’s finish the job together. | | | | | == | Peter, Today, I'm honored to announce that I'm officially running for Congress in Nevada's 1st District. Like so many of you, I've stood up against the D.C. establishment when they turned their backs on the American people. Even with President Trump back in the White House, judicial overreach by activist judges drags out our border crisis while Nevada needs MAGA fighters to bring jobs back, lower prices, and restore America's energy independence. | == And confidence in our elections remains at an all-time low. That's why I am leading the charge to take on the establishment in Congress. As a conservative businessman and former Nevada assemblyman, I've never been afraid to stand up to the D.C. swamp. I am running to FULLY BACK President Trump in securing borders and putting our Nevada citizens ABOVE special interests. But I can't get to Washington D.C. unless my campaign has the support of grassroots patriots like yourself. Can I count on you to stand with my America FIRST campaign and make a donation of $25, $50, $100, or any amount today? | == | == | == | == Every dollar donated to my campaign helps me stand up to the D.C. Swamp. Now is the time for Congress to begin delivering REAL results for our hardworking Nevada families. With President Trump back, we can finish the job together. Thank you for your support. | | Team -- Opponents of voting rights have made a strong bet. They've doubled down on it the last few years, too. Their bet was that we'd only care about certain states. That as long as we were focused on the so-called "swing states" like Arizona, Georgia, Pennsylvania, and others, that they would be free to suppress votes in states like Utah, South Dakota, Mississippi, or Kentucky. When Texas started messing with changes to voter ID requirements, people howled. clean_body: Opponents of voting rights are betting we'll ignore certain states| | | | | Team -- Opponents of voting rights have made a strong bet. They've doubled down on it the last few years, too. Their bet was that we'd only care about certain states. That as long as we were focused on the so-called "swing states" like Arizona, Georgia, Pennsylvania, and others, that they would be free to suppress votes in states like Utah, South Dakota, Mississippi, or Kentucky. And you know what? That bet has paid off for them. When Wisconsin tried to ban drop boxes, there was an immediate reaction and lawsuits. When South Dakota did the same? Crickets. When Texas started messing with changes to voter ID requirements, people howled. When Utah functionally suppressed the youth vote with new ID requirements? Very little response. They've created a feedback loop: states with restrictive voting laws receive little attention because they aren't electorally competitive. But part of the reason they aren’t competitive is because their state laws prevent large segments of the population from voting. If you've saved your payment information with FastAction, your donation will go through immediately: | | | | | | | | | | We're not going to lie -- when we've highlighted things in these things in the past , like voter ID in Utah or court decisions in Kansas or the most suppressive state voting law in Indiana, we haven't gotten much of a response from our supporters. People replied and said that we shouldn't waste our resources in those states, since they weren't important to the Electoral College, or a Senate election, or that we couldn't beat the vote suppressors there.The danger in ignoring the voting rights of citizens in more than half the country is that it creates a two-tiered democracy. Voters in the "swing states" benefit from attention and legal actions, while voters everywhere else are left to navigate increasingly onerous and burdensome requirements without meaningful support or scrutiny. We have to fight everywhere. Donald Trump is actively dismantling democratic institutions and undermining the rule of law. Only through free and fair elections can we hope to restore our republic. Peter, It’s been barely a month since we launched, but the energy I’m seeing across WI-03 makes it feel like we’re already in November. Folks are fed up with Derrick Van Orden and the chaos in Washington, and just want to see results that actually benefit us. We might be months from that big day, but that doesn’t mean our campaign is slowing down any time soon. We’re hard at work meeting voters in towns and cities across our district -- sharing the word about our efforts to bring real leadership to WI-03. Below are some highlights from recent events that I wanted to share. But first and foremost, I want to thank you, Peter. Your support keeps us doing this every day, and I’m more confident than ever that we can bring meaningful, working-class change to Congress. I hope to see you out on the trail, Rebecca | ****[Donate](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106307540/541091952/-2087246159?refcode=em-4.22.25-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85MzUwMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzMmNkNDU4Yy1hNjFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=eLa40HZ1ilZwTD3EEPgH0_p4uqpxVUsZllsha_Ujs7M=)****

* * *

**I stopped by Eau Claire County Democrats’ coffee klatch!** These folks meet weekly and keep our county party churning year round to elect Dems up and down the ballot. I’m grateful for their encouragement as we get out the gate to retire Derrick Van Orden.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106307541/541091953/-2087246159?refcode=em-4.22.25-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85MzUwMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzMmNkNDU4Yy1hNjFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=eLa40HZ1ilZwTD3EEPgH0_p4uqpxVUsZllsha_Ujs7M=)
**I joined La Crosse County Democrats’ membership drive** \- and this room was packed full of new faces (this photo doesn't do justice!) Year round organizing is what La Crosse Democrats are known for - they were hard at work all spring getting the vote out for Judge Crawford and so many local races!
** ** **[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106307543/541091955/-2087246159?refcode=em-4.22.25-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85MzUwMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzMmNkNDU4Yy1hNjFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=eLa40HZ1ilZwTD3EEPgH0_p4uqpxVUsZllsha_Ujs7M=)**
**US Mail? Not for sale. Proud to stand in solidarity with the American Postal Workers Union’s members and talk at their seminar in Eau Claire.** In Congress you can count on me to support the PRO Act and the Vote at Home Act and stand up against efforts to privatize the postal service.
**[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106307545/541091957/-2087246159?refcode=em-4.22.25-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85MzUwMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzMmNkNDU4Yy1hNjFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=eLa40HZ1ilZwTD3EEPgH0_p4uqpxVUsZllsha_Ujs7M=)**
**Felt the hometown love at one of our first events in Eau Claire.** Be sure to look out for events from roundtables, coffee, and more coming to your community soon. **[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106307547/541091959/-2087246159?refcode=em-4.22.25-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85MzUwMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzMmNkNDU4Yy1hNjFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=eLa40HZ1ilZwTD3EEPgH0_p4uqpxVUsZllsha_Ujs7M=)**
**And I took a rare break from campaigning and working to get to see the legendary Bob Dylan perform in Eau Claire!** Come senators, congressmen / Please heed the call /Don't stand in the doorway / Don't block up the hall
**[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106307548/541091960/-2087246159?refcode=em-4.22.25-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85MzUwMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzMmNkNDU4Yy1hNjFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=eLa40HZ1ilZwTD3EEPgH0_p4uqpxVUsZllsha_Ujs7M=)**
Every day, we are picking up the voters we need to win this race and flip WI-03. And I hope you’ll stick with us for the ride.

| | As a proud Oregonian, I have a deep, unwavering appreciation for the natural beauty of our state and the endless outdoor spaces and opportunities it has to offer. **That's why this Earth Day, I'm as committed as ever to protecting our great state's clean air, water, and land for future generations.** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106308251/541094770/-2044921950?refcode=2025-04-22-earth&recurring=0&amount=3&amounts=10,30,50,100,200&refcode2=88e2fe7b-a81f-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDEvMS84OTQxMiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4OGUyZmU3Yi1hODFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=cqbgRdrk9exoDOkCHgP_W-EmOQk8dsyIb4GDuy_GWcA=) To preserve Oregon's rivers, mountains, coasts, and valleys, _all of us_ must be a part of a greater movement to save our planet. We must tackle the climate crisis by moving toward a clean energy future. But today – 55 years since we first observed Earth Day – that future is deeply uncertain. Donald Trump has made it a priority to undo the clean energy progress we made through the Inflation Reduction Act. He's rolled back common-sense environmental protections and given big polluters the green light to move full speed ahead. He's emboldened climate deniers everywhere. **And earlier this month, he directed his Justice Department to block "****burdensome and ideologically motivated"****state and local efforts to address the climate crisis.** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106308252/541094771/-2044921950?refcode=2025-04-22-earth&recurring=0&amount=3&amounts=10,30,50,100,200&refcode2=88e2fe7b-a81f-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDEvMS84OTQxMiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4OGUyZmU3Yi1hODFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=cqbgRdrk9exoDOkCHgP_W-EmOQk8dsyIb4GDuy_GWcA=) We need a people-driven, grassroots movement at every level to fight against Trump's anti-climate actions and reverse the dangerous course our planet is on. We can't allow ourselves to give in to intimidation and massive corporate spending, and we cannot lose sight of this truth: **we still have the power to pass transformative environmental policies that secure our children's and grandchildren's future.** I'll never take my state, my country, or my planet for granted, and I remain committed to a world with opportunities that are sustainable. | | | | |
# Virtual Panel: Forecasting AI’s Workforce Impact
---
| | | | | | | | | | | Dear friends,
This week, we have some exciting news. ARI is bringing together a range of economic and tech policy experts across the political spectrum to share their thoughts on AI’s workforce impacts, and you’re invited.
Here’s the latest from ARI including our [upcoming virtual panel](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=5bba7db337&e=a07d75591f) on AI and the workforce.

---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
|
### AI’s WORKFORCE CROSSROADS
---
| | | | | | | | | | | Since ChatGPT’s debut, GenAI has evolved from a curiosity to an industry priority, accelerated by the rise of agentic systems. But a disconnect has emerged in conversations about the workforce impacts of AI’s diffusion. While some economists project manageable labor market changes based on historical patterns, others forecast that transformative capabilities will emerge as soon as 2027, displacing a large share of the workforce.
[**Register for our May 8 panel on AI’s workforce impact.**](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=eb1c6e1ce9&e=a07d75591f)
---
[](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=a9dd316146&e=a07d75591f)
| You may have seen our latest report, [The Technologist-Economist Disconnect: Assessing AI Labor Disruption](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=9351aa726a&e=a07d75591f), exploring the workforce impacts of artificial intelligence using a new framework for technological disruption.
Our upcoming virtual panel builds on that report by bringing renowned technology, labor, and industry leaders together for a conversation on the issue.
Joining the panel we have ARI’s own John Soroushian, Stanford Unviersity’s Erik Brynjolfsson, Crystal Weise from the AFL-CIO Tech Institute, and AEI’s Brent Orrell.
[Register for the Zoom Webinar here](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=1d7629f6b9&e=a07d75591f) or tune into our [X](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=3d6fd6170e&e=a07d75591f), [LinkedIn](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=d0feb4bdda&e=a07d75591f), or [YouTube](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=f0481ef09d&e=a07d75591f) for a livestream of the event!

---
| [VIRTUAL PANEL REGISTRATION ](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=1735b2ff96&e=a07d75591f)
---
|
---
|
### TAKE IT DOWN ACT GETS LEGAL BACKUP
---
| | | | | | | | | | | The TAKE IT DOWN Act, a bill to combat non-consensual AI-generated intimate imagery, is moving through Congress at lightning speed.
As the bill nears a House vote, ARI tapped former DOJ official Slade Bond to [write a legal memo](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=47f5653162&e=a07d75591f) defending the constitutionality of the TAKE IT DOWN Act and its alignment with the First Amendment.
Check out Bond’s legal memo supporting the TAKE IT DOWN Act [here](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=41f99c7568&e=a07d75591f).
ARI is expecting a vote on the TAKE IT DOWN Act next week. We’ll keep you up-to-date on its status.
---
| [](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=c7e1436fd7&e=a07d75591f)
---
| [SEE THE MEMO](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=ac33c6c5bc&e=a07d75591f)
---
|
---
|
### WHITE HOUSE RESTRICTS H20 CHIPS
---
| If you’ve missed the drama surrounding Nvidia’s H20 chips over the past week, we’re here to catch you up.
News began to break earlier this month that Chinese AI firms were [stockpiling Nvidia’s H20 chip](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=125f776f83&e=a07d75591f), a chip designed to provide enhanced inference capabilities for frontier AI models while staying just under U.S. export control thresholds.
Then, as the Trump administration considered updating export controls to stop China from acquiring H20s, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang flew to Mar-a-Lago for dinner with the president. After the tech executive made the case that Nvidia’s H20 should not be blocked, news leaked that the Trump administration might reverse course and allow the sale of $16 billion of H20 chips to China.
Americans for Responsible Innovation joined the fray and [called](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=c9df5c386a&e=a07d75591f) on the Department of Commerce to follow through on export controls stopping Nvidia’s H20 chip sales to China. ARI made the case that maintaining a tight hold on China’s chip bottleneck is critical to maintaining U.S. leadership on AI. [Read the full letter here](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=9c15170bb6&e=a07d75591f).
Finally, last week, the Trump Administration announced that it would, in fact, restrict H20 sales to China. Check out [our statement](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=4e87ed16c5&e=a07d75591f) applauding the Trump administration for its smart move on H20 export controls.

---
| | Our VP of Policy, Justin Bullock, recently joined a panel of experts at Columbia University’s Knight First Amendment Institute for a discussion on the transformative nature of AI and how it affects democratic freedoms.
He was joined by Google DeepMind’s Seb Krier, Humane Intelligence’s Rumman Chowdhury, and Centre for Governance of AI’s Sam Manning. The panel was moderated by the Knight Institute’s Seth Lazar.
Be sure to [watch our clip on X](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=9434f0c641&e=a07d75591f) and the [full panel discussion](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=002494f681&e=a07d75591f).

body:
#
On day one, Trump promised he would ‘end the Green New Deal.’
Since then, he’s announced plans to eliminate 31 Biden-era protections — and the jobs of 1,155 chemists, biologists, and other scientists — at the EPA.1

My name is Haley Stevens, and I’m running for Senate.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106309602/541099688/-436958700?refcode=EM_250422split_N_HS_90DO_17_G_N_P1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84Nzg0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNDk1OGFmOS1hYjFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=bUOdG5csMUp5z7vGs44DPjW8AI6j5cBI3DNotQOZzSg=) Hi, Peter – this is Congresswoman Haley Stevens writing to you with exciting news: Today, I’m launching my campaign for Michigan’s open U.S. Senate seat.

Winning in Michigan is essential to regaining our Democratic Senate majority, and right now The Cook Political Report is rating our race as a “Toss Up.” That means we’re already one of the GOP’s top targets for defeat. Just last year, they spent nearly $80 million trying to buy Michigan’s Senate seat and came up only 0.3% short, so I need your early support to win.

**Peter, I want to tell you a bit more about myself and why I’m running.** [**But if that’s all you needed to hear and you’re ready to get to work, please chip in whatever you can – split between my campaign and Shontel Brown – to help hit our $1 million launch goal and become a Founding Donor of my campaign to keep Michigan blue.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106309603/541099690/-436958700?refcode=EM_250422split_N_HS_90DO_17_G_N_L1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84Nzg0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNDk1OGFmOS1hYjFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=bUOdG5csMUp5z7vGs44DPjW8AI6j5cBI3DNotQOZzSg=)

I’m proud to be a lifelong Michigander. I learned the value of hard work by watching my parents – who owned their own landscaping business – build things. Heavy machinery equipment, bobcats, plows, dirt, grease, and grime – it was all part of my childhood.

Later in life, I got the call to give back to the state I love during a time of great uncertainty: the Great Recession. **I can’t tell you how unfathomable it was to hear the words “bankruptcy” and “General Motors” in the same sentence.** So I stepped up to do my part and served as chief of staff for the Auto Rescue initiative under President Obama.

We brought workers, corporations, and union leadership around the same table to stabilize the auto industry. On Friday nights, I’d stay in the office until the late evening and return every call from every Michigander who called our office worried about the future. _In the end, we saved 200,000 Michigan jobs._

I can’t help but see parallels between then and now as we find ourselves in another moment of great uncertainty, thanks to the chaos forced on us by Donald Trump and his billionaire buddy Elon Musk.

People are rightly concerned about rising costs, shoot-from-the-hip tariffs, and attacks on our personal freedoms. **Michiganders need a fighter in their corner – and that’s who I’ve been my entire life.**

[**If you’re ready to fight with me – to win this battleground race, take back the Senate majority, and stop Trump – can you split a grassroots donation between my campaign and Shontel Brown? Every dollar counts toward my $1 million campaign launch goal.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106309604/541099694/-436958700?refcode=EM_250422split_N_HS_90DO_17_G_N_L2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84Nzg0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNDk1OGFmOS1hYjFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=bUOdG5csMUp5z7vGs44DPjW8AI6j5cBI3DNotQOZzSg=) _If you’ve saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will be processed immediately and automatically split between Shontel Brown and Haley Stevens:_ | | [$1 »](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106309605/541099695/-436958700?refcode=EM_250422split_N_HS_90DO_17_G_N_EB1&express_lane=true&amount=1&refcode2=EL1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84Nzg0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNDk1OGFmOS1hYjFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=bUOdG5csMUp5z7vGs44DPjW8AI6j5cBI3DNotQOZzSg=)

clean_body: My name is Haley Stevens, and I’m running for Senate. = Hi, Peter – this is Congresswoman Haley Stevens writing to you with exciting news: Today, I’m launching my campaign for Michigan’s open U.S. Senate seat. Winning in Michigan is essential to regaining our Democratic Senate majority, and right now The Cook Political Report is rating our race as a “Toss Up.” That means we’re already one of the GOP’s top targets for defeat. Just last year, they spent nearly $80 million trying to buy Michigan’s Senate seat and came up only 0.3% short, so I need your early support to win. Peter, I want to tell you a bit more about myself and why I’m running. = I’m proud to be a lifelong Michigander. I learned the value of hard work by watching my parents – who owned their own landscaping business – build things. Heavy machinery equipment, bobcats, plows, dirt, grease, and grime – it was all part of my childhood. Later in life, I got the call to give back to the state I love during a time of great uncertainty: the Great Recession. I can’t tell you how unfathomable it was to hear the words “bankruptcy” and “General Motors” in the same sentence. So I stepped up to do my part and served as chief of staff for the Auto Rescue initiative under President Obama. We brought workers, corporations, and union leadership around the same table to stabilize the auto industry. On Friday nights, I’d stay in the office until the late evening and return every call from every Michigander who called our office worried about the future. In the end, we saved 200,000 Michigan jobs. I can’t help but see parallels between then and now as we find ourselves in another moment of great uncertainty, thanks to the chaos forced on us by Donald Trump and his billionaire buddy Elon Musk. People are rightly concerned about rising costs, shoot-from-the-hip tariffs, and attacks on our personal freedoms. Michiganders need a fighter in their corner – and that’s who I’ve been my entire life. = If you’ve saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will be processed immediately and automatically split between Shontel Brown and Haley Stevens: | | = | | = | = | | = | = | | = I know a thing or two about winning competitive races when the odds are stacked against me. Back in 2018, I flipped a battleground House seat from red to blue and helped usher in a Democratic majority to serve as a check on the first Trump administration. I was also just recognized as the most effective Michigan congressperson in the House. I’m taking that tenacity straight to the campaign trail. But I need you with me, Peter. Donald Trump’s handpicked candidate, Mike Rogers, is running again – and we know Republicans will spend tens of millions of dollars to buy this Senate seat for Trump. That’s why we must build the strongest possible campaign from day one: = Thank you for being a part of this team right from the get-go. I’m so grateful for your support. name: Yassamin Ansari
subject: 1 day, 3 town halls
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Yassamin Ansari for Congress
body:

Hi Peter, I got back to Phoenix last week for my district work period, and let me tell you, it’s been nonstop. My highest priority is hearing from Arizonans about their concerns and sharing exactly how I'm fighting for you in Congress. In fact, I did 3 town halls on Saturday alone! [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106311449/541105902/-1866165361?refcode=AU_YA_FR_GEN_NOA_AC_20250422_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA5NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlNTY4M2RmYy1iMTFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=mOlG3kfcmiXfi_wU5_9U57xcULYoi-zQQ2PPXU0GCVM=) We kicked off the day in Glendale, where I heard from residents concerned about the devastating Republican cuts to vital programs like Head Start and utility assistance. After that, I joined local, county, and state leaders at IBEW Local 640 for a town hall hosted by AFSCME, one of the labor unions that has been most targeted by the Trump Administration. I heard first-hand testimonies from union members who are struggling with the high cost of living that has been further exacerbated by Trump's reckless tariff policy. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106311453/541105910/-1866165361?refcode=AU_YA_FR_GEN_NOA_AC_20250422_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA5NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlNTY4M2RmYy1iMTFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=mOlG3kfcmiXfi_wU5_9U57xcULYoi-zQQ2PPXU0GCVM=) And finally, we rounded out the night in South Phoenix at Betty Fairfax High School, where I was proud to be joined by the ACLU of Arizona and the AZ Center for Economic Progress. Many members of our community expressed deep fear about ongoing mass deportations and the lack of due process most recently highlighted by the case of Kilmar Abrego Garcia. The fact that Donald Trump is refusing to comply with a Supreme Court order to facilitate his return to the United States is a deeply alarming, watershed moment in our country’s history. Hearing from so many of my constituents compelled me to travel to El Salvador to draw further attention to this constitutional crisis and demand that the Trump administration bring Kilmar home. I just got back and will share more details from my trip with you soon. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106311455/541105912/-1866165361?refcode=AU_YA_FR_GEN_NOA_AC_20250422_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA5NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlNTY4M2RmYy1iMTFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=mOlG3kfcmiXfi_wU5_9U57xcULYoi-zQQ2PPXU0GCVM=) I’m working tirelessly every single day on behalf of our community and our country. From hosting Know Your Rights trainings and town halls in every corner of AZ-03, to joining lawsuits against Trump and introducing my Affordability Agenda, I will continue to use every opportunity to fight boldly and fearlessly. Soon, I’ll be traveling to Republican districts to host town halls in their communities, too. **Because while Republicans are too scared to face their residents, I am not.** We need to be everywhere, all the time, and I’m committed to doing that. Thanks so much for all of your support. I couldn’t possibly do this work without you. Yassamin Ansari Congresswoman, AZ-03 | [DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106311457/541105995/-1866165361?refcode=AU_YA_FR_GEN_NOA_AC_20250422_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA5NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlNTY4M2RmYy1iMTFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=mOlG3kfcmiXfi_wU5_9U57xcULYoi-zQQ2PPXU0GCVM=)

That's why Hillsdale College is conducting a National Survey on Presidential Selection.

But today, more than a dozen states have joined together in an attempt to undermine this constitutional bulwark of liberty.

This movement to undermine the Constitution has grown largely because of the failure of America's schools to provide young people with a proper grounding in American civics—too many Americans simply don't understand the importance of the Constitution, including the Electoral College, to liberty.

Because of this, Hillsdale College has expanded its educational mission on behalf of liberty nationwide, directly teaching millions of Americans in all 50 states.

These efforts, which aim to counter the Left's domination over most of our schools, include:

Teaching millions of citizens nationwide through free online courses, such as "Constitution 101" and "The Great American Story: A Land of Hope;"

Reaching over six million households and businesses nationwide with Imprimis, Hillsdale's free digest of liberty;

Promoting constitutional education through social media outlets popular with young people;

Sending millions of pocket-size copies of America's founding documents to citizens and K-12 schools across America; and

Restoring excellence to K-12 education by helping establish and guiding classical K-12 schools nationwide and providing, free of charge, Hillsdale's American classical K-12 curriculum (including American civics) to thousands of American educators and homeschoolers.

Your answers to the National Survey on Presidential Selection will help Hillsdale form the most effective strategy to educate millions of Americans about the importance of the Constitution to liberty—including the importance of the Electoral College.

Our race is already a toss up, and I need your early support to win

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106311798/541106895/2126292383?amount=25&refcode=email_042225_stevens&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3MTJlYjQ2ZC1iMzFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=uAhdW7_MzlI73zlQ-aoVjDILVkGESyuPUsDXt9H2rnM=) Hi – this is Congresswoman Haley Stevens writing to you with exciting news: Today, I’m launching my campaign for Michigan’s open U.S. Senate seat. Winning in Michigan is essential to regaining our Democratic Senate majority, and right now The Cook Political Report is rating our race as a “Toss Up.” That means we’re _already_ one of the GOP’s top targets for defeat. Just last year, they spent nearly $80 million trying to buy Michigan’s Senate seat and came up only 0.3% short, so I need your early support to win. **I want to tell you a bit more about myself and why I’m running.[But if that’s all you needed to hear and you’re ready to get to work, please chip in whatever you can – split between my campaign and Andrea Salinas – to help hit our $1 million launch goal and become a Founding Donor of my campaign to keep Michigan blue.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106311799/541106896/2126292383?amount=25&refcode=email_042225_stevens&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3MTJlYjQ2ZC1iMzFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=uAhdW7_MzlI73zlQ-aoVjDILVkGESyuPUsDXt9H2rnM=)** | | [CHIP IN →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106311800/541106897/2126292383?amount=25&refcode=email_042225_stevens&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3MTJlYjQ2ZC1iMzFmLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=uAhdW7_MzlI73zlQ-aoVjDILVkGESyuPUsDXt9H2rnM=)

I’m proud to be a lifelong Michigander. I learned the value of hard work by watching my parents – who owned their own landscaping business – build things. Heavy machinery equipment, bobcats, plows, dirt, grease, and grime – it was all part of my childhood.
Later in life, I got the call to give back to the state I love during a time of great uncertainty: the Great Recession. **I can’t tell you how unfathomable it was to hear the words “bankruptcy” and “General Motors” in the same sentence.** So I stepped up to do my part and served as chief of staff for the Auto Rescue initiative under President Obama.
We brought workers, corporations, and union leadership around the same table to stabilize the auto industry. On Friday nights, I’d stay in the office until the late evening and return every call from every Michigander who called our office worried about the future. _In the end, we saved 200,000 Michigan jobs._
I can’t help but see parallels between then and now as we find ourselves in another moment of great uncertainty, thanks to the chaos forced on us by Donald Trump and his billionaire buddy Elon Musk.
People are rightly concerned about rising costs, shoot-from-the-hip tariffs, and attacks on our personal freedoms. **Michiganders need a fighter in their corner – and that’s who I’ve been my entire life.**

"**Man accused of shooting Deputy Sheila Jones in downtown Houston courthouse shootout is identified** " Houston Chronicle's **John Wayne Ferguson** \-- "The man accused of [shooting a Harris County deputy constable in downtown Houston](https://substack.com/redirect/aa1631d8-7cb2-4d97-b75a-364212d85c19?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Monday afternoon was identified Tuesday morning in charging documents accusing him of aggravated assault of a public servant and unlawful carrying of a weapon.

**Parnell Bland** , 34, of Houston, is accused of shooting Precinct 1 deputy constable **Sheila Jones** , according to court records. Jones survived the shooting after a bullet was stopped by her ballistic vest, officials said Monday.

Five deputies approached Bland Monday afternoon after receiving a call about a weapons disturbance near the Harris County Family Law Center. Bland, who authorities said was carrying two handguns, allegedly fled from the deputies before turning and firing a shot at Jones. The deputies returned fire, striking Bland multiple times.

Bullets from the shootout also shattered a window at the county's jury assembly building and broke a pane in a county office building. Only Bland and Jones were hit. Both were expected to survive, officials said.

Bland could ultimately face more assault charges for firing on the each of the deputies who responded to the call, as well as other possible gun charges, Harris County District Attorney **Sean Teare** said Monday.

Bland's criminal history in Harris County includes six felony convictions, three of which were for possession of cocaine. His most recent conviction was for theft in 2018. Bland pleaded guilty and was sentenced to 18 months in state jail. Felons aren't allowed to own or carry weapons in public in Texas.

Bland also has a record of misdemeanor and felony arrests in Liberty County dating back to 2016, including convictions for drug possession, DWI and trespassing. His most recent arrest in Liberty County was in October, when he was sentenced to 45 days in jail on a trespassing charge, according to court records.

On April 15, Bland was also charged with misdemeanor criminal trespass. He was scheduled to appear in Harris County Criminal Court at Law No. 3 on Tuesday morning on that charge.

Officials on Monday didn't speculate why Bland brought the guns downtown or where he might have been going before police were called. Precinct 1 Constable **Allen Rosen** said Bland may have mental health issues, but didn't elaborate.

Court records show that in 2018, Bland was ordered to receive mental health treatment and be restored to competency before facing his felony theft charge. He was deemed fit to stand trial after around 7 months of treatment.

Bland was being treated for his wounds as of Monday, and on Tuesday was not yet listed as being in custody at the Harris County Jail. He was scheduled to make a preliminary appearance in front of a Harris County district judge on Wednesday. Prosecutors have already asked for a hearing to be scheduled so they may argue for Bland's bail to be denied." "**Man accused of shooting Deputy Sheila Jones in downtown Houston courthouse shootout is identified** " Houston Chronicle's **John Wayne Ferguson** \-- "The man accused of [shooting a Harris County deputy constable in downtown Houston](https://substack.com/redirect/7a576d26-b007-4603-b821-575b24e09e2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Monday afternoon was identified Tuesday morning in charging documents accusing him of aggravated assault of a public servant and unlawful carrying of a weapon.

**Parnell Bland** , 34, of Houston, is accused of shooting Precinct 1 deputy constable **Sheila Jones** , according to court records. Jones survived the shooting after a bullet was stopped by her ballistic vest, officials said Monday.

Five deputies approached Bland Monday afternoon after receiving a call about a weapons disturbance near the Harris County Family Law Center. Bland, who authorities said was carrying two handguns, allegedly fled from the deputies before turning and firing a shot at Jones. The deputies returned fire, striking Bland multiple times.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $7/mo](https://substack.com/redirect/267e4c12-92be-4a0f-917e-0e5c5450608f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Bullets from the shootout also shattered a window at the county's jury assembly building and broke a pane in a county office building. Only Bland and Jones were hit. Both were expected to survive, officials said.

Bland could ultimately face more assault charges for firing on the each of the deputies who responded to the call, as well as other possible gun charges, Harris County District Attorney **Sean Teare** said Monday.

Bland's criminal history in Harris County includes six felony convictions, three of which were for possession of cocaine. His most recent conviction was for theft in 2018. Bland pleaded guilty and was sentenced to 18 months in state jail. Felons aren't allowed to own or carry weapons in public in Texas.

Bland also has a record of misdemeanor and felony arrests in Liberty County dating back to 2016, including convictions for drug possession, DWI and trespassing. His most recent arrest in Liberty County was in October, when he was sentenced to 45 days in jail on a trespassing charge, according to court records.

On April 15, Bland was also charged with misdemeanor criminal trespass. He was scheduled to appear in Harris County Criminal Court at Law No. 3 on Tuesday morning on that charge.

Officials on Monday didn't speculate why Bland brought the guns downtown or where he might have been going before police were called. Precinct 1 Constable **Allen Rosen** said Bland may have mental health issues, but didn't elaborate.

Court records show that in 2018, Bland was ordered to receive mental health treatment and be restored to competency before facing his felony theft charge. He was deemed fit to stand trial after around 7 months of treatment.

Bland was being treated for his wounds as of Monday, and on Tuesday was not yet listed as being in custody at the Harris County Jail. He was scheduled to make a preliminary appearance in front of a Harris County district judge on Wednesday. Prosecutors have already asked for a hearing to be scheduled so they may argue for Bland's bail to be denied." TOP NEWS "Man accused of shooting Deputy Sheila Jones in downtown Houston courthouse shootout is identified " Houston Chronicle's John Wayne Ferguson \-- "The man accused of Monday afternoon was identified Tuesday morning in charging documents accusing him of aggravated assault of a public servant and unlawful carrying of a weapon. Parnell Bland , 34, of Houston, is accused of shooting Precinct 1 deputy constable Sheila Jones , according to court records. Jones survived the shooting after a bullet was stopped by her ballistic vest, officials said Monday. Five deputies approached Bland Monday afternoon after receiving a call about a weapons disturbance near the Harris County Family Law Center. Bland, who authorities said was carrying two handguns, allegedly fled from the deputies before turning and firing a shot at Jones. The deputies returned fire, striking Bland multiple times. Bullets from the shootout also shattered a window at the county's jury assembly building and broke a pane in a county office building. Only Bland and Jones were hit. Both were expected to survive, officials said. Bland could ultimately face more assault charges for firing on the each of the deputies who responded to the call, as well as other possible gun charges, Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare said Monday. Bland's criminal history in Harris County includes six felony convictions, three of which were for possession of cocaine. His most recent conviction was for theft in 2018. Bland pleaded guilty and was sentenced to 18 months in state jail. Felons aren't allowed to own or carry weapons in public in Texas. Bland also has a record of misdemeanor and felony arrests in Liberty County dating back to 2016, including convictions for drug possession, DWI and trespassing. His most recent arrest in Liberty County was in October, when he was sentenced to 45 days in jail on a trespassing charge, according to court records. On April 15, Bland was also charged with misdemeanor criminal trespass. He was scheduled to appear in Harris County Criminal Court at Law No. 3 on Tuesday morning on that charge. Officials on Monday didn't speculate why Bland brought the guns downtown or where he might have been going before police were called. Precinct 1 Constable Allen Rosen said Bland may have mental health issues, but didn't elaborate. Court records show that in 2018, Bland was ordered to receive mental health treatment and be restored to competency before facing his felony theft charge. He was deemed fit to stand trial after around 7 months of treatment. Bland was being treated for his wounds as of Monday, and on Tuesday was not yet listed as being in custody at the Harris County Jail. He was scheduled to make a preliminary appearance in front of a Harris County district judge on Wednesday. Prosecutors have already asked for a hearing to be scheduled so they may argue for Bland's bail to be denied." [ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/62?t=1001&akid=8499%2E5257348%2ERsctJJ ]Adam Schiff for Senate

Derek,

Protecting the Earth for my kids and yours has been one of my top
priorities all the way back to the early days of my career.

After law school, a clerkship, and a brief stint in private practice, I
went to work for the United States Attorney’s Office as an Assistant U.S.
Attorney. During my time there, I fought to hold polluters and toxic waste
dumpers accountable for violating environmental laws. My work there even
led to the creation of the first federal environmental crimes unit in Los
Angeles.

My work to protect our planet continued as a member of the California
State Senate and later as a member of the U.S. House. I led the way in
expanding light rail in Southern California, helped establish California’s
earthquake early warning system, and championed legislation to preserve
and protect California’s natural beauty and public lands.

And now, I’m serving on the Environment and Public Works Committee as a
United States Senator, where I continue to advocate in the strongest terms
for bold action to tackle climate change and grow our economy.

But the current administration is downright hostile to any attempts to
protect our environment.

Donald Trump is not only refusing to address the climate crisis, but he’s
actively making it worse every day. He’s making it as easy as possible for
polluters, fossil fuel companies, and toxic waste dumpers to make our air
dirtier and water less clean.

The science is clear — we need to take strong action to mitigate the worst
impacts of climate change and protect our planet, public lands, and the
environment.

That’s why I’ve supported the Green New Deal and worked to build a green
economy that will create millions of new jobs, lower energy prices for
working families, make American energy independent, and dramatically
expand clean energy technologies.

Frankly, we don’t have any other choice. The Earth is warming to
potentially catastrophic levels, and the United States must be a global
leader in the fight to reduce emissions and transition to a green economy.
